- In the lead-up to the 2026 midterm elections, the Alaska Senate race was embroiled in controversy as a claim circulated that Democrats engaged in ballot-stacking, referring to an election tactic where political parties recruit additional candidates to draw votes away from an opponent
- Alaska Democrats allegedly pushed a candidate named Dan J. Sullivan to run for Senate in order to confuse voters and direct votes away from Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, the Republican incumbent. Snopes readers asked us to determine the veracity of this claim and the legality of such a tactic.
- The rumor stems from a New York Times investigation based on the claims of an ex-employee of Democratic candidate Mary Peltola, interviews with dozens of people involved and a review of communications and documents. We have no reason to doubt the veracity of the Times' reporting. However, because we were unable to view the evidence or obtain additional confirmation from people involved, we cannot confirm its claims as of this writing.
- Snopes concluded that even if Peltola's team engaged in ballot-stacking, it's not unprecedented. Republicans have also employed the tactic during elections. U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche also said that such actions "should be" illegal but stopped short of saying they are. The Alaska Supreme Court has permitted the independent candidate Sullivan to run on Nov. 3.
- Election expert John Fortier told Snopes that while people have been prosecuted for deceiving voters, there is no specific law related to the process of ballot-stacking.
- Snopes will update this report if additional information surfaces. We have reached out to Peltola's and incumbent senator's campaigns, as well as independent candidate Sullivan and members of the team allegedly involved in the stacking plan, and await responses.
In an investigation published Oct. 28, The New York Times reported that staffers for Alaska Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola spent months recruiting candidates named Dan Sullivan in order to peel votes from incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan.
Political parties often employ the election tactic, referred to as "ballot-stacking," to confuse voters by deliberately recruiting additional candidates to run with the goal of drawing votes away from an opponent.
In Alaska, a candidate named Dan J. Sullivan, whom a Democratic operative associated with Peltola's team allegedly recruited, is on the ballot, alongside Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan. President Donald Trump has called Peltola's alleged actions a "fraud on the American public." Additionally, the Department of Justice filed a lawsuit to block or delay the election certification if the incumbent were to lose the senate race.
Snopes readers asked us to look into the legality of ballot-stacking as an election tactic, as well as the veracity of the claim that Peltola's staffers tried to recruit multiple Dan Sullivans to join the Senate race. Readers also wanted to know whether the DOJ could block the election from being certified if the Republican candidate lost.
Below we break down everything we know about the controversy and ballot-stacking during elections:
Did Peltola's team carry out ballot-stacking?
The New York Times spoke to Elisa Rios, a former staffer and campaign manager for Peltola who was recently fired. Rios claimed top campaign aides instructed her to find as many people named "Dan Sullivan" as they could in Alaska and convince them to run for Senate, causing confusion among voters and possibly costing the incumbent senator crucial votes.
The Times reported that it reviewed text messages and conducted numerous interviews with Rios and 12 people who participated in the alleged plan, knew about the plan or were would-be candidates. Shortly before the story was published, Rios attempted to retract her statements to the Times, the newspaper reported. She was planning to file a wrongful-termination lawsuit against the Peltola campaign. The Times kept her statements in the story.
The Peltola campaign denied being involved in Dan J. Sullivan's candidacy. Jim Lottsfeldt, a local political consultant aligned with super PACs supporting Peltola, said Rios was a source of "disgruntled, anti-Mary Peltola stuff that I think is often not true." The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee also denied participating in such a project, but the Times said it had reviewed texts and documents showing otherwise.
Rios claimed a Democrat operative named Jerid Kurtz — who reportedly posed as a man named "Zane" and approached people to attempt to convince them to run in or to drop out of the race — made contact with Dan J. Sullivan and described him as amenable to running if it would help Peltola.  Kurtz is an Ohio native, according to the Times, and would reach out to people under the alias with an email that included the word "buckeye." Ohio is known as the Buckeye State.  
Rios also alleged that Jacquelyn Lopez, an attorney for the Peltola campaign, was involved in efforts to create a "right-wing state party" that could challenge the incumbent Republican senator.
We have no reason to doubt the veracity of the Times' reporting. However, because we were unable to view the evidence or obtain additional confirmation from people involved, we cannot confirm its claims as of this writing.
Snopes reached out to an individual we believe to be Rios via Facebook and will update this story if we receive a response We have also reached out to Lopez but did not receive a response by the time of publication. We were unable to contact Kurtz, who has removed his social media pages.
Additionally, we contacted Peltola's campaign to learn more and will update this story accordingly.
Ultimately, Dan J. Sullivan is allowed to run in the Senate election,
Who is Dan J. Sullivan and is he allowed to run?
Daniel J. Sullivan, a retired teacher, lives in the small fishing community of Petersburg, according to the Times. He is contesting the Nov. 3 senate election with no party affiliation, though he initially registered to run as a Republican. Sullivan has maintained publicly that he entered the Senate race of his own volition, though Rios contended that he was contacted by Kurtz and expressed a desire to help Peltola's campaign.
We reached out to Sullivan to learn more about the motivations behind his candidacy. We will update this story if we receive a response.
As of June 26, Sullivan is legally permitted to run in the election — something that the Peltola campaign and its affiliates celebrated, according to the Times' report — though the election board initially attempted to block him.
On June 15, the Alaska Division of Elections announced that Sullivan was ineligible to participate and would be removed from the ballot because his filing was "for the purpose of confusing or misleading voters." Carol Beecher, the elections division director, wrote in a letter (emphasis ours):
You requested to access the ballot under the name "Dan Sullivan" even though it appears from Division records that you have never registered to vote or sought ballot access under this name. Our records indicate that you are registered to vote under the name "Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr." That you chose the occasion of your declaration of candidacy for U.S. Senate to seek ballot access under a name you have not used in your interactions with the Division suggests—and in combination with the additional facts I outline in this letter leads me to conclude—that you are seeking to confuse yourself with another candidate in the race, the incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan, rather than distinguish yourself from him. Indeed, you yourself appeared to be confused when you initially emailed the Division asking to be listed on the ballot as "Dan S. Sullivan." "S" is Senator Sullivan's middle initial, not yours.
She added, in a likely reference to Kurtz:
A political consultant you have admitted is working with your campaign is a known longtime supporter of Democratic candidates including the primary Democratic challenger to Senator Sullivan. This consultant's work on your behalf is, in isolation, innocuous. Alongside the other facts I have catalogued in this letter, however, it suggests a determined effort and a deliberate attempt to use the similarity of your name to confuse Alaska voters in the upcoming primary election.
Upon appeal, on June 26, the Alaska Supreme Court permitted Sullivan to appear on the ballot, though it did not give its reasoning. Alaskan Republican officials made the decision about how Sullivan was to appear on the ballot, and determined he would be listed without a party affiliation while the incumbent senator would be listed as a Republican. Alaskan voters can vote for both men if they are confused between the two, as the election employs a ranked-choice system. 
Is ballot-stacking illegal?
Generally, ballot-stacking as an election tactic is not illegal. In a Fox News interview, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche called the practice fraud. When asked whether the practice was illegal, Blanche said "it should be" but stopped short of saying it actually was.
The Times investigation also noted that "ballot-stacking tactics are common in politics and generally considered legal."
For example, in 2024, according to an Alaska News Source report, a registered Democrat named Eric Hafner ran for Alaska's U.S. House seat, even though he was incarcerated in a federal prison in New York and did not even live in Alaska. (Hafner had been sentenced to 20 years in prison for making death threats to judges, police officers and others.)
The Alaska Beacon noted that while the Democratic Party sued to keep Hafner off the ballot, the Republican Party sought to keep him on it. The Alaska Supreme Court ruled in Hafner's favor and the Republican candidate defeated Peltola for the House seat. Hafner's campaign advertising was also reportedly backed by a Republican campaign group.
Also in 2024, a pro-Peltola PAC ran ads for a third-party candidate after Democratic strategists saw the tactic as favorable to Peltola.
John Fortier, a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, a right-leaning think tank, told Snopes over the phone that there is no specific law against adding similar-sounding names to ballots as an election tactic. However, there have been cases where people were prosecuted on grounds of deceiving voters, Fortier said, like cases filed against groups accused of making deceptive "robocalls" to voters to spread false information about election dates.
For example, in 2011, a campaign manager for Republican former Maryland Gov. Robert Ehrlich was convicted of two counts of conspiracy to violate election laws and two counts of election fraud. He orchestrated a scheme of robocalls targeting Black Democratic voters by informing them that Democratic Gov. Martin O' Malley had already won the election as of 6 p.m. on Election Day 2010, and thus attempted to deter them from going to the polls.
We also found a 2020 case in Florida where a local Republican Party chairman was found guilty of a misdemeanor campaign finance violation through a scheme in which he planned to use a so-called ghost candidate to siphon votes away from the Republican candidates' competitor.
Can DOJ delay or block election certification process?
On Oct. 22, the DOJ filed a complaint against the state of Alaska, Beecher, the state election board and the state ballot counting review board, saying the sole purpose of Dan J. Sullivan's candidacy was to "benefit the Peltola campaign by reducing the number of votes for Senator Sullivan." The lawsuit sought to delay or block Alaska from certifying its election results if the Republican candidate lost.
Fortier told Snopes that the DOJ complaint did not have a "real leg to stand on [as] the grounds were not really clear." He said, generally speaking, it is uncommon for election certification to be delayed or overturned, and even more uncommon for federal actions to be imposed on a state's election. The DOJ complaint appeared to be geared towards "broadly raising the issue [of ballot-stacking] and putting it back into people's minds," he added.
The U.S. Constitution allows states to control their own elections, so the DOJ lawsuit may have little merit in the long run. Additionally, Alaska's ranked-choice voting system means it could take weeks to finalize a result.
The state argued thst the DOJ lawsuit had "no legal basis," adding that "delaying certification of Alaska's election results—but only if a particular candidate does not win—would interfere with state election administration and threaten election integrity." The state also noted that the ballots now clearly distinguish the two candidates, who are now listed as "Daniel J. Sullivan Jr." with no party affiliation, while the incumbent is listed as "Dan S. Sullivan."
The state's response said:
If any voter remains confused, Alaska law allows voters to receive assistance from others. And if the voter is still uncertain, he can rank both Sullivans as his first and second choices under Alaska's ranked-choice voting system so that his vote will count for either Sullivan over any other candidate.
Will it affect the election?
Some Alaskans say such political tactics will do little to change their views. An Alaska Public Media report featured interviews with Alaskans on both sides of the aisle. One registered Republican said he was still voting for Peltola and that Rios' claims were likely because she was a disgruntled former employee.
Another voter said, "Voters are intelligent and can figure out how to rank and can figure out which Dan Sullivan is their person."
Some Petersburg locals also described Dan J. Sullivan as a man of "high character" and did not believe the Times' account of him working with Democrats behind the scenes.
In sum …
While The New York Times' reporting indicates Democrats in Alaska may have engaged in political skullduggery, ballot-stacking appears to be a common tactic employed many times by both sides over the years with minor repercussions. Even the U.S. attorney general said such a practice "should be" illegal but did not assert it was.
As of this writing, both Sullivans are on the ballot for the Nov. 3 Senate election in Alaska.

New research shared exclusively with Kernel Panic shows that hackers have started adding AI functionality into a new strain of infostealer malware, making it possible for the system to automatically profile victims and quickly surface the highest value targets and their information. Dubbed “Volta-Autodoxer” because of how the malware refers to itself internally, the finding by Cisco Talos researchers sheds light on the ways that commercial LLMs are being used to augment and enhance the capabilities of established types of malware.
Often hidden in counterfeit software, infostealers are designed to live up to their name, grabbing usernames, passwords, authentication tokens, cookies, credit card data, and more from infected machines. Many of the biggest data breaches in recent years—from the widespread Snowflake-linked breaches that included AT&T and Ticketmaster to the theft of a terabyte of Disney data—have resulted from hackers accessing targets using login details gathered by infostealers. Overall, the malware has been used to steal hundreds of millions of credentials in recent years.
“Volta is pretty mature as a stealer. It casts a pretty wide net for what it collects,” says Ryan Fetterman, a security researcher at Cisco Talos. “It compiles all of those things together, ultimately producing a serialized dossier that it can send to a couple LLM models. It’s asking the model to act like an intelligence analyst and produce structured citation-backed assessment of the victim. It’s like a prioritization and analysis function.”
Talos flagged the malware using its new CAIRN framework, built to identify hacking tools that incorporate AI capabilities. Fetterman notes that Talos did not track whether Volta has been used in the wild.
Volta’s traditional infostealer capabilities are powerful and seem to be geared toward targeting younger internet users with robust digital lives. It sweeps for passwords stored in browsers, Microsoft OAuth tokens, cookies, payment cards, and crypto wallet seed phrases, but also active Discord, Telegram, Steam, and Roblox sessions. Then the malware does a second, deeper sweep using its first-round findings. By looking through the target’s Gmail or another central account, Volta builds a fuller picture of the victim, their location, and their habits using data like receipts and order history from services including UberEats and DoorDash.
Once all of this is done, the malware feeds its findings into AI tools for analysis using OpenRouter, a service that can send prompts to multiple different AI providers. Volta defaults its requests to Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6. But apparently preparing for the possibility that the model’s guardrails could block the activity, Volta is built with fallbacks to the Chinese open weight Moonshot AI Kimi K2 and, if that fails, Google’s Gemini 2.5 Flash. Building in fallbacks and relying on cost-effective, older-generation models are common techniques among attackers.
Volta’s creators included a 240-word prompt, including bullet points and a numbered list, as part of their instructions to any LLM analyzing the collected data. “You are a forensic intelligence analyst drafting a target assessment from a structured evidence bundle,” the Volta prompt says. It instructs the chatbot to produce an “executive summary” about the person, details of what they do, “what they’re worth,” and a summary of “their opsec.” It adds that the chatbot should “connect dots across fields,” for example, checking whether someone’s Wi-Fi password matches their last name. “Go deep, not wide,” the prompt says.
“The prompt is pretty carefully crafted not to imply anything overtly malicious,” Fetterman says. “But they’re building in the expectation to potentially hit model refusals at first request. And so they plan for failover kind of cascading to more permissible models as they go down the chain. And there’s also the capability to still use the implant without the AI. The AI calls are kind of above and beyond, but the malware will still work without it.”
Some low-level cybercriminals and scammers have complained about AI slop filling up cybercrime forums, but security researchers are increasingly discovering other hackers using LLMs for coding tasks or analyzing troves of stolen information. Researchers at threat intelligence firm Crowdstrike, for example, recently told WIRED they had seen four distinct hacking groups with varying sophistication—operating in Chinese, Spanish and English, Indonesian, and Russian—using AI tools to compromise dozens of targets around the world, including government entities and businesses in health care, retail, and travel.
Cisco’s Fetterman says Volta contains some clues that it may have been built to sell to a range of attackers rather than being developed for one specific actor’s campaigns. And while the malware at its core is still a traditional infostealer, the AI expansion foreshadows even more invasive and sinister activity in the future.
“If you’re able to identify your high-value targets faster, you probably have a better chance of using their credentials or authenticating using stolen tokens more often than maybe you would have if you had to do that triage yourself,” Fetterman says, referencing the fact that authentication tokens expire and passwords can be changed. “We’re seeing more advanced capabilities accessible to lower-level sophistication attackers. It’s really interesting and disturbing.”

Samsung's Galaxy Ring gets FDA approval for advanced sleep apnea detection
The upgraded feature uses AI to detect the number of breathing disruptions for every hour you sleep.
Samsung's Galaxy Ring now offers more advanced sleep apnea detection following FDA approval of the new feature in July, the company announced. The feature may give users new clues about why they feel exhausted even after sleeping through the night.
Samsung first received so-called De Novo FDA authorization for sleep apnea detection on its Galaxy Watch and Galaxy Ring devices back in February 2024. (De Novo is used for health products or features that have never been on the market before and don't pose any danger to a user's health.) The original approval only covered detection for symptoms of moderate to severe sleep apnea.
The new version does that, but also uses AI to detect the frequency of breathing disruptions for every hour you sleep. Provided you sleep at least five hours for two nights over a ten-day period, Samsung's Health Monitor app can tell you if you have mild, occasional or frequent sleep apnea. Samsung points out that only a physician can do a proper sleep apnea diagnosis, but the device "can lead to productive conversations with healthcare professionals."
Neither of Samsung's primary Galaxy Ring competitors, Oura and Superhuman, offer FDA-approved sleep apnea detection. However, both can track nighttime disturbances that may indicate signs of the condition. Samsung and Oura are currently locked in a legal dispute over smart ring patents, with a preliminary decision expected to be handed down soon.
Along with the Galaxy Ring, the advanced sleep apnea detection feature is now available on the Galaxy Watch 9 with Wear OS 7.0 or later. It will also come to the Galaxy Watch 7 and Galaxy Watch 8 through software updates down the road. If you need further help with your slumber, Samsung recently revamped its Sleep Coaching feature to require less data than before.

Chennai-based stroke medicine expert Sivarajan Thandeswaran has called for certification of Indian hospitals to distinguish them as ‘stroke-ready’ so that people do not waste time in seeking treatment.
“Hospitals in India have to apply for and obtain NABH or JCI certification; instead, a proper government legislation making it mandatory for patients to be taken to and treated at comprehensive stroke centres, as done in the West, will improve stroke care,” said a senior consultant in Stroke Medicine, General Internal Medicine and Gerontology, at Kauvery Hospital in Alwarpet on Wednesday.
He was speaking at a webinar on ‘The Golden Hour: Every Minute Matters, Every Life Counts’, presented by Kauvery Hospital in association with The Hindu to mark World Stroke Day, observed annually on October 29.
He was joined by Harish R. Kamath, consultant neurologist, Kauvery Hosur. The experts stressed on the need for timely access to care as time is the most crucial factor to salvage the brain. Stroke is the second leading cause of death and, therefore, treatment in the window period of 4.5 hours is critical.
Treatment of stroke has transformed tremendously, and families need to be aware, Dr. Thandeswaran added.
In his presentation, Dr. Kamath explained the symptoms of stroke, including loss of balance, blurring vision, facial asymmetry, weakness in arms, and slurring speech. He said 1.8 million new stroke cases are added every year and 7.25 million deaths due to stroke occur every year.
Dr. Thandeswaran said that while big city hospitals have facilities for scanning, imaging, and treatment, including thrombolysis (dissolving blood clots with medicine) and thrombectomy (removing clot through surgery), in remote areas, telemedicine and video calls were being used in identifying stroke patients and transferring them to Comprehensive Stroke Centres, where advanced services and specialist teams are available.
The doctors discussed lifestyle-related risks, including poor dietary habits, physical inactivity, and inadequate sleep.
“People should take ownership of their health through routine check-ups for better treatment outcomes,” Dr. Thandeswaran suggested.

In a major setback to Jammu and Kashmir's ruling National Conference (NC), Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi on Monday announced his decision to quit the party and resign from the Lok Sabha, accusing its leadership of betraying the people's mandate and failing to fulfil electoral promises.
Ruhullah made the announcement during a public gathering organised in Budgam to mark the death anniversary of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi. A large number of supporters gathered at the Behesht-e-Zahra Park for the event.
Ruhullah announces resignation at Budgam gathering
Displaying his resignation to the gathering, the MP declared that he was stepping down and described his decision as an 'Azadinama'. He submitted his resignation from the party through Mohammad Ashraf Mattu.
Before announcing his decision, Ruhullah launched a sharp attack on Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, saying that the chair he occupied had become a source of distress for everyone. He further alleged that Omar did not need to place his cap and dignity at the feet of others to protect his position and power.
Accuses NC of betraying electoral promises
Explaining his decision, Ruhullah said his differences with the party leadership were ideological and political rather than personal. He accused the National Conference of failing to honour its commitments on the restoration of Article 370, protection of constitutional rights, reservation policy and the release of prisoners lodged in jails.
He maintained that compromising on these issues was not an option for him, as the party had sought public support on the basis of these very promises.
Plans new political platform
Ruhullah also clarified that he was not planning to join another political party. Instead, he intends to build a new political platform by bringing together honest, committed and politically aware youth who understand the concerns of Jammu and Kashmir and want to work towards social change.
Meanwhile, his Lok Sabha seat will not become vacant immediately. His resignation will have to be formally accepted by the Lok Sabha Speaker before the Srinagar constituency can be declared vacant and a by-election initiated under the relevant legal provisions.

Afcon to return to two-year cycle after Caf U-turn
- Published
The Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle after a U-turn from the Confederation of African Football (Caf).
In December, Caf announced that the tournament would be held every four years instead, but that decision has been reversed after a review.
Under the new plans, the governing body was planning an African Nations League to replace Afcon as its biennial tournament, but acknowledged that it would take several years to generate the revenue required to become self-sufficient.
"The decision by the Executive Committee to reinstate the organisation of the Afcon every two years aims to advance, protect and promote the interests of African football and the 54 Caf Member Associations, as well as those of African players playing for clubs outside the continent," Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in a statement.
The biennial hosting of Afcon has long caused issues with the football calendar, with the vast majority of recent tournaments held midway through the European club season.
Fifa's expanded 32-team Club World Cup was held in June and July last year, which also forced Caf to opt for mid-season dates.
The next Afcon will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament, followed by editions in 2028, 2031 and 2033. There will be no tournament in 2030 because of the World Cup.
The dramatic 2025 Afcon final saw Senegal crowned champions before they were stripped of their title three months later in favour of Morocco.

The easiest way to turn your regular TV into a smart TV
You don't need a fancy new TV to access smart features.
As the world of streaming and online entertainment has slowly become an integral, seemingly permanent part of our daily lives, the actual act of accessing all the content you want to see has become as wide open as it could possibly be. There are so many options out there for insanely high-end smart TVs, and the people making them are already trying to figure out how to make even more expensive ones.
Each new smart TV promises to be better than the last one, but for some folks out there, the concept of even buying one doesn't sound very smart at all. Maybe you don't like the expense, or maybe you have a TV you really like and want to find a way to enhance it instead of investing in a new one. It ultimately doesn't matter what your reasoning is, because no matter how you slice it, it's a sound option.
Transforming a regular TV into a smart TV is actually surprisingly simple and, perhaps more compelling, affordable. All you really need is a TV that fits the bill and the right streaming stick for you, and you're all set up for the smart TV experience.
Find an HDMI port on your TV
Your first order of business in determining if you can turn your older TV into a smart TV is to make sure it has the appropriate slots to do so. In most cases, a simple HDMI port will do the trick, and you can check for them on the back. They can be on either side of the unit, sometimes directly in the middle if your TV has a larger back.
Annoyingly, some TVs come with the HDMI ports facing in an awkward direction that makes plugging something in a bit frustrating. It's rare, but if you find yourself unable to find an HDMI port, you can check to see if it's just in an odd position. If your TV really doesn't have an HDMI port, yet it has the old-school RCA inputs or an RF input, there are several adapters that make converting to a smart TV possible.
Once you've found a proper HDMI port, you'll need to grab yourself something like an Amazon Fire TV Stick or one of the many options available to you. These are tiny units that plug directly into your HDMI port; then you can simply tune your TV to that input, and you're off to the races. You'll need to log into all of your streaming services, but once that's done, you'll be good to go.
Buying a streaming stick vs. a smart TV
Buying a streaming stick has its own advantages that make it a worthwhile option. To start with, they're all generally less expensive than an actual smart TV. Most streaming sticks or hubs can be as cheap as $30, while a cheap smart TV can set you back as much as $150 on the lower end of things. It's also a lot more convenient, and most streaming sticks are more or less plug-and-play.
If you're absolutely committed to holding onto your old TV, there's nothing wrong with that, and you have a lot of options to turn it into a smart TV. If the TV is substantially older, however, or if you're helping a senior get set up, then it may be in your best interest to go for the smart TV.
It's becoming increasingly difficult to actually find non-smart TVs in stores today, and you can certainly still find them if you look hard enough, but that may not be true in the years to come. If you're just in the market for a decent smart TV to watch streaming content on, look for something from Roku or Samsung, both of which have excellent accessibility options for those who have hearing loss or low vision.

Keralam Health Minister K. Muraleedharan on Friday said the government would take further action after receiving a report from an expert committee probing the allegations that expired doses of Remdesivir were administered to Nipah patients in previous years.
However, critical care specialist Dr A S Anoop Kumar, who treated several Nipah patients at a private hospital, said that patients who died due to Nipah were not administered doses of Remdesivir.
Former Health Minister Veena George said that allegations raised by Mr. Muraleedharan are suspicious as the medicine has an expiry period of 2.5 to 5 years.
In a reply to a submission by Congress MLA Mathew Kuzhalnadan in the Assembly on Thursday, Mr. Muraleedharan said that Remdesivir procured in 2021 had an expiry date of May 2023 but might have been administered to patients admitted to Kozhikode Medical College till 2025.
Speaking to reporters in Kozhikode, Mr. Muraleedharan said the information presented to the Assembly was based on reports from responsible officials of the Health Department and that he would not make further comments until the expert committee submitted its findings.
The government would investigate whether the deaths of Nipah patients were linked to the administration of expired medicine and whether other patients who received the drug had suffered any adverse effects, Mr Muraleedharan said.
“There are several doubts regarding the medicine, including whether it was administered after its expiry date. We will investigate and take a decision,” he said.
The Minister clarified that there were no concerns about the quality or efficacy of Remdesivir itself and that the issue under investigation was whether expired doses had been administered to patients.
Recalling the procurement of the drug during the Nipah outbreak after the UDF government came to power, he said efforts to source it from different parts of the country had failed as the available stocks in Mumbai had expired.
Subsequently, the Kerala Medical Services Corporation Limited (KMSCL) informed the government that the medicine was available in Bahrain, following which it was procured within 48 hours, he said.
He said patients who received the medicine within its validity period had recovered and asserted that the controversy concerned its expiry date rather than the drug’s efficacy.
Mr. Muraleedharan said the expert committee headed by Dr R Aravind, head of the Infectious Diseases department at Thiruvananthapuram Medical College, would conduct an impartial examination without any preconceived conclusions.
The probe would also examine how the medicine was procured and supplied, the role of intermediaries and the functioning of KMSCL.
The government would investigate whether any agents were involved in the procurement process, he said.
The Minister also said the Kozhikode Medical College superintendent had informed him that the packaging of the Remdesivir medicine listed an expiry date but did not mention its manufacturing date. Both details are normally required on medicine packaging, and the discrepancy would be examined, he said.
“Further decisions on the issues would be taken after receiving the expert committee’s findings,” he said.

Rallying-Double world champion Rovanpera returns to WRC in expanded Toyota lineup
Nov 3 : Two-time champion Kalle Rovanpera will return to the world rally championship with Toyota next year after leaving in 2025 to try his hand at circuit racing, the Japanese manufacturer said on Tuesday.
The 26-year-old Finn will do a partial season, allowing other drivers including France's nine-times world champion Sebastien Ogier to compete in selected events.
"I’m enjoying having the chance to do some different things, but rallying has been a huge part of my life and I naturally started to miss the driving after a while," Rovanpera said in a statement.
• Rovanpera became the youngest world rally champion aged 22 in 2022 and left last year to explore other possibilities. Medical issues put his circuit racing plans on hold.
• He will be joined by Estonia's Ott Tanak, who was champion with Toyota in 2019 and is returning after a year out.
• Toyota will run two distinct teams, with two different cars and a total of six drivers in a new rules era.
• The Toyota Racing team will feature Britain's 2026 champion Elfyn Evans, Sweden's Oliver Solberg and Finland's Sami Pajari and debut the new Celica Rally1 car.
• Gazoo Racing Toyota will compete with the new GR Yaris, driven by Rovanpera, Tanak and Japan's Takamoto Katsuta.
• Toyota took a record-equalling sixth consecutive manufacturers’ championship this year.

Shares of insurtech major PB Fintech hit a fresh 52-week low today, plunging about 8% to ₹926 apiece on the BSE. The stock closed the day’s trading session 7.19% lower at ₹928.10 apiece on the BSE. The company’s stock is down 48% since September 23, since the IRDAI floated its consultation paper to overhaul the insurance distribution industry Its market capitalisation stood at ₹42,948.08 Cr ($4.53 Bn). PB Fintech commanded a market cap of $9.07 Bn at the end of the first week of September, over twice of its market cap now. The dip today comes after the company’s quarterly disclosures last Friday. PB Fintech’s consolidated net profit rose 42.5% YoY to ₹192.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹135 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, profit increased 18% from ₹163 Cr in Q1 FY27. Operating revenue grew nearly 35% YoY to ₹2,177.7 Cr, from ₹1,613.6 Cr in Q2 FY26. It rose 15% sequentially from ₹1,888.3 Cr in the June quarter. While total income stood at ₹2,277.6 Cr, total expenses increased 32.6% YoY to ₹2,067.7 Cr. The company’s core online business, which includes Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, generated ₹1,336 Cr in revenue, up 39.5% YoY. Revenue from new initiatives rose 28% YoY to ₹842 Cr. Adjusted EBITDA increased 39% to ₹216 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA margin remained flat YoY at 10% Brokerages have given mixed outlooks for the stock post the disclosures. HSBC and Dolat Capital retained their ‘Hold’ and ‘Reduce’ ratings, respectively, while Bernstein maintained its ‘Outperform’ call. HSBC kept its target price at ₹1,100 but cut its FY27-29 earnings per share (EPS) estimates by 2-4%, citing higher operating costs and regulatory uncertainty. Bernstein retained its target price of ₹1,085, citing 38% YoY growth in consolidated premiums and 22% growth in core credit disbursements. Dolat Capital retained its ‘Reduce’ rating but cut its target price to ₹1,090 from ₹1,150. The brokerage said Q2 revenue rose 35% YoY to ₹2,177.7 Cr but was 4.2% below its estimate. EBIT also missed estimates by 32.7%, mainly due to higher advertising and other expenses. It flagged concerns that proposed IRDAI rules could reduce insurance distribution payouts and affect PB Fintech’s PoSP model. Dolat cut its FY27-FY29 EPS estimates by 3%, 3.9% and 4.1%, respectively, due to uncertainty over the impact of the proposed rules. PB Fintech’s Future Outlook PB Fintech has said its PoSP insurance distribution business may need to be restructured if the IRDAI’s proposed rules are adopted in their current form. During the earnings call, chairman and CEO Yashish Dahiya said the proposals could limit the scope of the existing PoSP model. The company will wait for the final regulations before deciding on its next steps. Dahiya said PB Fintech was in informal discussions with the regulator about other options, which it would announce only after receiving certain regulatory approval. He added that the proposals could open up opportunities to offer non-insurance services, including potentially charging for claims support that Policybazaar currently provides for free, subject to the final rules. PB Fintech has begun reducing costs, with hiring in October at a “very, very small fraction” of earlier levels, the management said. The company also plans to move existing executives into newer businesses and use AI to improve efficiency. Advertising and promotion expenses rose 59% YoY to ₹447 Cr in Q2, outpacing revenue growth. Core credit disbursements rose 22% YoY to ₹2,791 Cr but were broadly flat sequentially. Management said it had focused on adding lending partners before pursuing further growth.

A mother’s knowledge, attitude and feeding practices can significantly influence a child’s willingness to try new foods, which highlights the need for stronger nutrition counselling for caregivers during early childhood, according to a new study by researchers at the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (NIN).
Reluctance to try unfamiliar or diverse foods studied
The study, published in the Journal of Nutritional Science, examined food neophobia, a condition in which children are reluctant to try unfamiliar or diverse foods. Such behaviour can limit dietary variety and potentially affect nutritional health during crucial years of growth.
Researchers assessed 150 mother-child pairs from Addagutta in Hyderabad between August and October 2025 focusing on children aged two- seven years and explored how maternal feeding practices were associated with food neophobia and children’s nutritional status.
Findings
The findings revealed that nearly 77% of children showed moderate levels of food neophobia, while 11.3% displayed high levels and 12% had low levels. Boys recorded slightly higher food neophobia scores than girls, although the differences were not statistically significant.
Nutritional status-food acceptance link
The study also found a link between nutritional status and food acceptance. Children suffering from wasting were more likely to exhibit higher food neophobia scores than those with normal nutritional status, suggesting that reluctance to try new foods may be associated with poorer dietary outcomes.
Nutrition knowledge an important factor
Researchers observed that maternal knowledge, attitudes and practices played an important role. Children whose mothers demonstrated moderate levels of nutrition-related knowledge and positive feeding practices had lower food neophobia scores than those whose mothers had lower scores.
Karthikeyan Ramanujam, Scientist-C at ICMR-NIN and lead author of the study, said the findings underscore the importance of everyday feeding behaviours. He suggested that caregivers should repeatedly offer a variety of foods without pressure, create positive mealtime experiences and respond supportively when children reject unfamiliar foods.
ICMR-NIN Director Bharati Kulkarni said the findings offer an opportunity to strengthen behavioural feeding counselling through existing government programmes such as the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) and POSHAN Abhiyaan.
Researchers cautioned that the study was limited to a single urban low-income community and a relatively small sample size. They noted that, as a cross-sectional study, it identifies associations but cannot establish direct cause-and-effect relationships, as per a press release.

East Bengal’s profligacy in front of goal proved costly as Omani side Al Seeb scored twice in the closing stages to register a 2-0 victory in their Group D fixture of the AFC Champions League Two at the Salt Lake Stadium on Tuesday.
Despite dominating possession and creating several clear-cut opportunities, the Red and Gold Brigade failed to find the breakthrough, with Axel Meye and Zahir Sulaiman striking late to secure all three points for the visitor.
East Bengal started on the front foot, dictating the tempo with its passing game. Dani Ramirez came close in the 10th minute after Edmund flicked the ball through to Rashid, who picked out the Spaniard on the edge of the box. Ramirez’s left-footed effort narrowly missed the right post.
The host threatened again in the 20th minute when Al Seeb goalkeeper Ibrahim Al Mukhaini saved Edmund’s effort from close range. Bipin Singh collected the rebound and returned the ball into the danger area, but captain Rashid headed it wide.
Ramirez tested Ibrahim once more in the 33rd minute, but Ibrahim produced an excellent diving save to his right. East Bengal also suffered an early setback when defensive leader Anwar Ali sustained an injury and was replaced by Sandip Mandi in the 18th minute.
AS IT HAPPENED | EAST BENGAL VS AL SEEB HIGHLIGHTS
Despite its attacking superiority, East Bengal went into the break goalless. Al Seeb threatened after the restart, with Meye heading over from close range following a corner in the 48th minute. East Bengal responded in the 61st minute when Ramirez attempted to poke home after a move involving Jay Gupta and substitute Ake Loba, but Ibrahim produced another outstanding save.
At the other end, East Bengal goalkeeper Phurba Lachenpa denied Al Seeb midfielder Omer Almalki with a sharp reflex save in the 76th minute after a cross from substitute Zahir. East Bengal’s inability to convert its chances eventually proved decisive. Meye broke the deadlock in the 85th minute, controlling Hassan Al-Ajmi’s cross before getting past Mandi and firing home.
Al Seeb sealed the victory in stoppage time when Meye turned provider, releasing Zahir down the left. The substitute raced into the penalty area before calmly slotting the ball into the bottom-right corner in the 90+1 minute.
East Bengal head coach Antonio Habas’ team selection also raised questions, with three of the six registered foreign players initially left on the bench. Foreign forwards Loba and Lukasz Zwolinski were introduced midway through the second half, but their inclusion failed to change the outcome as the hosts continued to struggle in the attacking third.
The defeat left East Bengal bottom of Group D with two points, while Al Seeb climbed to third with four.
The result was particularly disappointing for East Bengal, which had earlier secured creditable ‘away’ draws against Jordan’s Al Hussein SC (2-2) and Al-Seeb (0-0).
However, consecutive home defeats against Iraq’s Al Shorta SC (3-2) and Al Seeb have exposed its inability to translate attacking promise into results. East Bengal’s lack of clinical finishing remains a major concern as its continental campaign falters.

TOI Correspondent From Washington:
 Americans are streaming into polling stations across the country on Tuesday in one of the most consequential midterm elections in modern U.S history, with Donald Trump facing the prospect of losing control of Congress and spending the final two years of a lame duck presidency negotiating with an opposition that has plenty of scores to settle. The MAGA boss used his closing campaign appearance rhapsodizing about the renovation of the Lincoln Reflecting Pool, a fittingly ironic finale to a campaign built around his promise to drain the swamp. By Tuesday night (Wednesday morning IST), if polls are correct -- and they often aren't -- he may discover that his own political fortunes are sinking.
Trump's closing appearance was billed as a final midterm appeal to voters agitated by war and cost of living issues, but the 53-minute event often resembled a municipal contractor's presentation to a homeowners' association. Rather than delivering a reassuring economic and political argument, he walked his audience through the pool's renovation, complete with photographs, elaborate explanations of the plumbing issues, and some outright falsehoods, leaving political pundits slack-jawed at the tone-deaf approach to the elections where Republicans are on the backfoot.
It was a bizarre climax to a campaign in which the MAGA supremo barnstormed roughly 20 states, addressing more than 30 rallies at which, in his own words, he “ranted and raved” in marathon two-hour speeches while treating congressional elections as a personal referendum despite asserting he is not on the ballot.
Latest surveys suggests voters may be preparing to hand the President and his party a pasting, with one model by pollster Nate Silver giving Democrats roughly a 95 per cent chance of capturing the House and an 80 per cent chance of taking the Senate. Prediction market Kalshi has put Democrats winning the House at about 93 percent odds and taking the Senate at 71 percent.
Headlines in major U.S newspapers include: "A terrible night awaits the GOP, and even that might be an understatement," "Democrats can’t believe their luck. No, really, they can’t" and "Five tell-tale signs of a Democratic blowout."
However polls measure intentions, not votes. Republicans are counting on Trump's ability to mobilise his loyalists in the final hours, while Democrats are hoping that the discontent reflected in surveys translates into actual ballots. If, however, Republicans do lose both chambers as is being widely projected, Trump will enter the final two years of his presidency in territory familiar to three recent predecessors, though none approached the prospect with quite his combination of combativeness and appetite for confrontation.
Barack Obama experienced the most recent equivalent after the 2014 midterms, when Republicans took the Senate and strengthened their House majority, leaving a Democratic President facing a Congress controlled entirely by the opposition. The result was legislative gridlock, with the most consequential episode coming in 2016, when Obama nominated Merrick Garland to the Supreme Court following Antonin Scalia's death. Senate Republicans, led by Mitch McConnell, refused even to schedule confirmation hearings, arguing that the vacancy should be filled by the next president. Garland's nomination expired without a vote.
It was an extraordinary exercise of Senate power, with consequences that extended far beyond Obama's remaining months. Trump subsequently nominated Neil Gorsuch for the vacancy, and it ultimately helped reshape the Supreme Court for a generation.
Similarly, George W. Bush ran into a Democrat-controlled House and Senate after the 2006 midterms, in the final two years of his presidency. The political backdrop was the deeply unpopular Iraq war, declining confidence in his administration and growing public dissatisfaction. Democrats used their congressional majorities to intensify oversight, challenge the administration's Iraq policy and push domestic legislation. Bush nevertheless negotiated on some issues, including the minimum wage and other measures, while foreign policy issues like the U.S-India nuclear deal found bipartisan support, demonstrating that divided government need not mean complete paralysis.
Bill Clinton had perhaps the longest and most instructive experience of being hamstrung by a congressional opposition. After the 1994 "Republican Revolution," he faced the formidable speakership of Newt Gingrich in a relationship that was hardly cordial. It produced two government shutdowns in 1995-96, a succession of bruising legislative confrontations and, eventually, Clinton's impeachment in 1998. His political survival and high approval rating towards the end of his term demonstrated that an opposition-controlled Congress can sometimes become an opportunity for a president to reposition himself as a pragmatic centrist.
No one is holding their breath about Trump adopting this course although he likes to present himself as a master deal-maker and negotiator. Past records and current form points to a man who prefers winning to finding compromises, and his instinct is to attack opponents, question their legitimacy, and turn political disagreements into personal vendettas. A Democratic Congress could therefore mean investigations, subpoenas, aggressive oversight of the administration and a near-constant battle over budgets, appointments and executive authority.

Centre can step in on airfares in rare cases, say new rules
The new rules shift the intervention power on specified tariff-related grounds from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to the Central Government.
The Centre can directly intervene on ticket pricing in extraordinary situations under a new set of aviation rules that also require airlines to disclose cancellation charges and refund conditions separately while displaying airfares to passengers.
These rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2024, were notified by the civil aviation ministry (MoCA) on October 26 and published in the Gazette of India on October 31. They will come into effect on January 1, 2027, replacing the Aircraft Rules, 1937. The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, which replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934, came into force on January 1, 2025.
The new rules shift the intervention power on specified tariff-related grounds from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to the Central Government. Under Rule 135(4) of the Aircraft Rules, 1937, the DGCA could issue directions to an airline if it was satisfied that the airline was charging excessive tariff. A new rule, 192(6), however, empowers the Central government itself to issue written directions in the public interest when it considers a situation extraordinary and intervention necessary. Such directions must be proportionate to the circumstances and remain in force only for a specified period, the rules say.

The provisions do not introduce a routine cap on airfares or require government approval for every ticket price. Hence, airlines will continue to determine fares in normal circumstances. The new framework, however, provides for tariff submission and monitoring by the DGCA.

Total amount payable by passenger
Under the new rules, airlines will have to show the total amount payable by a passenger on their booking websites and on the booked ticket, along with a complete break-up indicating the fare, taxes, fees, cancellation charges, refund conditions and any other charges separately.
The requirement applies to Indian airlines operating scheduled services as well as foreign airlines operating scheduled flights to, from, or across India. All such airlines will also have to publish their tariffs on their websites or other digital platforms in a specified format.

Cost of operation
The rules also require airlines to establish tariffs based on factors including the cost of operation. Indian scheduled airlines will have to submit their tariffs to DGCA, which will monitor the prices.
The new provisions build on disclosure requirements that already existed under the Aircraft Rules, 1937. The earlier rules required airlines to display the total amount payable by passengers and its break-up, including the fare, taxes, fees and other charges. The 2026 rules explicitly include cancellation charges and refund conditions in the list of particulars that must be displayed.

As the protests and hunger strike continues to unfold at Delhi’s Jamia Millia Islamia, students on October 27, Tuesday, reported a near-complete shutdown of normal university activities with the campus has being turned into a fortress surrounded by police personnel and tear gas vans deployed outside the main gate.
Additionally, Section 163 of the BNSS has been invoked, criminalising gatherings of more than four people. A warning sign erected by South-East District of Delhi Police mentions that unlawful gathering or assembly will be dispersed using physical force and legal action will be initiated.
Why are the Students Protesting?
On October 12, two students, Jasim Ali Khan and Ebin Basil, began an indefinite hunger strike to demand the resumption of the student union elections, which have not been held for two decades. The last elected union was dissolved in March 2006 amid allegations of campus violence and disruption. The university has not had a restored, university-wide elected Jamia Millia Islamia Student Union (JMI-SU) since then.
View this post on Instagram
Representatives from various student organisations submitted a memorandum to the vice-chancellor, demanding that necessary facilities, space, and support must be provided to students for their democratic right of free expression and protest. Within the next few days, six more students, Rehan Khan, Rehan Haider, Faizan Ali Khan, Rida Nausheen Khan, Ritik, Altaf, and Abuzar, joined the hunger strike and several students joined the sit-in demonstration around the Mirza Ghalib statue on campus. What followed is severe police crackdown, administrative retaliation, and a state-sanctioned attempt to curb what students described as a peaceful protest for their rights.
‘Students Beaten, Dragged & Detained’
Five days into the protest, around 5:30 am on October 17, Delhi Police personnel arrived in large numbers outside the university gate, and allegedly detained at least 10 students with the aid of the campus security guards. Students alleged that authorities turned off the lights, beat and dragged the protesters out of the campus in the break of dawn in the presence of the chief proctor of the university.
CPI(ML) Liberation alleged that Jamia Millia Islamia administration forcibly removed students on hunger strike from the campus around 5:30 am on Saturday while they were demanding the restoration of the students’ union. In a post on X, the party alleged that campus lights were switched off and students were beaten, manhandled and harassed before being handed over to Delhi Police. It said all detained students had since been released. The students are demanding the restoration of Jamia’s students’ union and the holding of union elections. CPI(ML) Liberation condemned the alleged action and urged the administration to stop what it called repression and restore the union.

Footage surfacing on social media showed clashes between authorities and the students protesters on the morning of October 17, with videos showing police dragging and pulling students away from the campus.
View this post on Instagram
A video also showed Ebin Basil, writhing in pain, alleging that he had been brutally assaulted by the security guards.
Subsequently, as scenes of utter chaos kept emerging through the day, a large group of students were seen breaking the gate and storming inside the campus even as the police reportedly denied detaining anyone and only removing those attempting to break the gate.
View this post on Instagram
Admin Condemns Slogans, Shifts Classes Online
On October 18, a high-level committee comprising seven university professors was formed to mediate between protesting students, and to convince them to call the demonstration off. During this meeting certain slogans that were painted on walls by students also came under the administration’s scrutiny. These slogans included ‘Restore JMISU’, ‘Reclaim Jamia’, ‘Inquilab Ayega’, ‘Free Palestine’, ‘Free Sharjeel Imam’, and ‘RSS Se Azaadi’ among others.
In a press release published by the official handle of the university on X, the slogans were labelled “highly condemnable and detrimental to the nation’s integrity, security and sovereignty.” The release further stated that the administration has adopted two resolutions. First, to urge the protesters to vacate the protest site and call off their agitation, particularly at the Ghalib statue lawns, which they claimed had been “illegally occupied by the protesting students despite Gate No. 18 being the designated protest site at JMI”. Second, “to repaint the defaced walls and cover the slogans”.
The press release added that the administration had been compelled to issue a notification to shift all classes online allegedly due to the protesters’ resistance to call off the demonstration. “After two hours of efforts to persuade the students to call off the protest…the students continued chanting slogans, shouting that the faculty should “go back” and suddenly began pushing security guards, staff and teachers…even after their demands had been met earlier this week,” the release stated.
Further, the university administration took disciplinary action against Ebin and Jasim. Ebin was rusticated for one academic year and barred from campus while Jasim Khan was barred from campus for six months.
Following the administrative action, students held a press conference on October 18 and expanded their demands beyond the restoration of the JMI-SU — they demanded the withdrawal of disciplinary proceedings against protesting students and an end to further punitive measures. They also demanded the resignation of the chief proctor and security advisor.
Students Vow to Continue Strike, Clampdown Increases
Even as certain hunger strikers gave up due to declining health, the remaining students vowed to continue their hunger strike and sit-in protests. Solidarity for the protesting students poured in from within and beyond the campus, however, the police deployment outside the campus and administrative clampdown also intensified.
“The irony lies in the fact that the same administration that condemned unauthorised police clampdown on students during the CAA-NRC protests in 2019 is deploying that very body against its students in 2026 to suppress the constitutionally safeguarded right of free and independent expression,” Ateerah, a post-graduate student, told Alt News.
On October 23, Congress MP Imran Masood was detained by Delhi Police after he arrived at the university to express solidarity with protesting students.
Water, Electricity, Basic Amenities Cut Off
On October 24 — the 13th day of the hunger strike — through another notice the administration shifted all classes to online mode, shut its gates, suspended canteen services, and restricted access to the Central Library. In what students viewed as an attempt to discourage the protest, electricity and water supply were also cut off in the campus space, students told Alt News. “They have essentially converted our dissent into a question of law and order, to justify police action on a peaceful protest,” said Abdul, another student.
On the same day, a large number of Delhi Police personnel and paramilitary forces were stationed outside the university premises. The protesting students told Alt News that in the afternoon, the proctor’s team, along with university professors and non-teaching staff, had rounded up students who had gathered for a sit-in demonstration within Gate No. 7 of the university premises, at the Ghalib Lawn.
Students alleged use of force on both male and female protestors by the security guards. The protest site was allegedly dismantled, which compelled the protesting students to take shelter within the Political Science building and continue their hunger strike, they added.
View this post on Instagram
Mantasha, a post-graduate student, told Alt News, “The whole affair was an unpleasant reminder of what had transpired within the university premises in 2019. This time, our own professors joined in with the security guards. Some just watched, while others proceeded to manhandle us. Until our 13th day of protest, a solitary female washroom was kept open at night. However, after the protest site was dismantled in the afternoon of October 24, we found that it had been sealed off, leaving us no option but to share the male washroom.”
Students Reject Admin’s Notification
The next day, on October 25, the administration released a notification that said that a student election would be held after 15 days from the date of approval of the constitution of the JMI-SU.
It stated that show cause notices and suspension orders against students during the period of protest would be revoked, and a committee would be constituted to enquire into the actions of the security staff. It also added that students should issue a public apology for any defamatory statement, action, or posts made during the protest against the administration.
However, students expressed their apprehension regarding the notification, pointing out that the date of constitution of the union was unspecified. Those on hunger strike continued their fast, deeming the notification an incomplete victory as all of their demands had not yet been addressed.
They demanded an assurance on the resignation of the chief proctor and the security advisor, and the revocation of all disciplinary actions on protesting students, besides declining to issue a public apology. “The Constitution of the union is to be drafted by December 20, after which it is subject to approval from the V-C. This allows a lot of scope for administrative inaction and complacency, since the approval itself can be indefinitely stalled by the administration,” alleged Abdul.
On October 26, two gates — one in front of the Ibn-e-Sina reading library, and another which serves as a key access point to the campus for residents of the Boys Hostel — were sealed off by the administration, with the suspension of offline classes still effective.
A student protestor, speaking on terms of anonymity, told Alt News, “The gate provides access to facilities serving not only students and hostel residents but also members of the general public, including an Indian Post Office, a public sector bank, an Aadhaar centre, a university health centre and a dental hospital. Restricting access to such essential public services, including medical care for patients with scheduled appointments, warrants immediate reconsideration.”
Less than 24 hours after the administration released the notice, Delhi Police however went on to detain several students for merely attempting to enter the premises of their own university, students told Alt News. Video footage showed police personnel pushing students onto a detention bus.
Speaking to Alt News from the protest site, students alleged that they are not being able to leave the campus given the heavy police and paramilitary deployment in front of the gates. Food and water deliveries are allegedly being intercepted by security guards at the gates, cutting off the basic means of survival for students who have remained within the campus.
“We had earlier put out a message asking for people in solidarity to send in drinking water, but the guards would not let it through. Is this how a university treats its students?” a student, requesting anonymity, asked.

WHO, the United Nations Foundation and Illumination have partnered to launch a Public Service Announcement (PSA) that reinforces safe and healthy practices during these challenging times, featuring Illumination’s globally beloved Gru and the Minions. The PSA focuses on lifesaving behaviors to help mitigate the impacts of COVID-19, including physical distancing, being active at home and remaining kind to each other —all aimed at making sure people of all ages stay safe and healthy during this pandemic.
“At this challenging time, we must find all ways possible to provide hope to people while sharing advice that can protect our health,” said Dr. Tedros Adhanom, Director-General of the World Health Organization. “WHO is excited to be working with Illumination and Steve Carell and the joys of the Minions and Gru to promote the importance of physical distancing, keeping active and connected, and being kind and compassionate to overcome COVID-19.”
The PSA is voiced by Academy Award® and Emmy Award® nominee Steve Carrell, who voices the character Gru in the Despicable Me franchise. The PSA will be localized into multiple languages including Spanish, French, Portuguese and Arabic, among others.
“Storytelling is a powerful tool to accelerate positive social change in the world. It is an honor to partner with the WHO and UN Foundation to remind people around the globe to protect themselves, each other and our communities during this pandemic. I am also appreciative to Participant for helping to organize the collaboration and to my partners at Comcast/NBCU for helping to amplify this important message,” said Illumination Founder and CEO Chris Meledandri.
Illumination is the first Hollywood Studio to partner with WHO, the UN Foundation and the COVID-19 Solidarity Response Fund to create an entertaining and educational PSA for global audiences. Participant helped facilitate the collaboration between Illumination to the United Nations Foundation and the World Health Organization.
"As the world continues to grapple with the challenges of COVID-19, one of our most powerful weapons is kindness," said Elizabeth Cousens, President & CEO of the United Nations Foundation. "We are delighted that the Despicable Me characters are letting their love show and showing ways to keep themselves and their communities safe during this unprecedented time."

3 appear in court accused of causing Athens gas explosion by stealing copper piping
Three men accused of causing a deadly explosion in Athens by stealing copper piping from a gas supply network are appearing in court for a preliminary hearing
ATHENS, Greece -- Three men accused of causing a deadly explosion in the heart of Athens’ tourist district by allegedly stealing copper piping from the local gas supply network were appearing in court Monday for a preliminary hearing.
The massive blast on Sept. 25 caused the collapse of a two-story residential building in the Greek capital’s historic Plaka district, near the ancient Acropolis. Six people were killed – an elderly couple living in one of the apartments, and four American tourists staying in a short-term rental property in the building.
The three suspects – two Greeks and one Albanian national – allegedly removed piping from the building’s gas supply network to sell the copper as scrap. The fire department announced on Thursday that a 34-day investigation led authorities to issue arrest warrants for the three for causing a major gas leak by allegedly stealing sections of copper piping.
“I’m devastated by what happened, but the explosion wasn’t my fault,” one of the three said when waiting reporters asked the suspects if they were sorry, as police led them into the courthouse.
Copper has high scrap metal value, and the theft of copper wiring, piping and metal from infrastructure sites in Greece is frequent.
The suspects face a series of serious charges, including arson, manslaughter with possible intent, causing a deadly explosion and causing dangerous bodily harm.

Quick Answer
The best free alternatives to popular Microsoft apps include LibreOffice for Microsoft 365, ShareX for Snipping Tool, Files for File Explorer, Everything for Windows Search, System Informer for Task Manager, and ImageGlass for Microsoft Photos. These offer more features, better speed, and greater control.
Microsoft bundles plenty of apps with Windows, and you probably use a bunch of them on your PC — some out of personal preference, others because there aren’t enough good alternatives.
Now, there’s nothing wrong with using these apps if they serve you well. But if you find their functionality limited or want a free version, you don’t have to settle. Here are some of the best free alternatives to popular Windows apps that are worth checking out.
Table of Contents
LibreOffice for Microsoft 365
Microsoft 365 is a subscription service that gives you access to Office, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams, alongside 1 TB of OneDrive storage. You can get Microsoft 365 for free, but you need a paid subscription for unrestricted access. However, if you don’t wish to go that route and want unrestricted access to the office suite, LibreOffice is a solid Microsoft 365 alternative worth checking out.
LibreOffice doesn’t require an account or subscription; you can download the app and get started right away. The suite includes three tools — Writer, Calc, and Impress, which are free equivalents to Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, respectively. You also get a vector graphics editor (Draw), a database management system (Base), and a mathematical formulas and equations editor (Math). The app works completely offline and stores all your data locally on the device. It doesn’t have any AI features either, so you have full control over what you do.
ShareX for Snipping Tool
Windows has a built-in screenshot tool called Snipping Tool to help you take screenshots and record the screen. Although Microsoft has updated it over the years to include OCR/text extraction and screen recording capabilities, its functionality is still largely limited compared to many third-party screenshot apps. ShareX is one such app, which is quite popular among power users.
ShareX offers plenty of screenshot modes, including scrolling capture, active monitor, custom, and auto-capture, as well as those you get with the Snipping Tool. Scrolling capture and auto-capture are two standout modes here. The former comes in handy when you want to capture content that extends beyond what’s visible on the screen. On the other hand, the latter lets you automatically take screenshots of a specified area at set intervals, which may be useful when you want to document the steps or monitor some process.
However, that’s not all; ShareX is better than Windows Snipping Tool at a bunch of other things. For example, it supports batch operations and automation capabilities. This allows you to apply edits to a bunch of screenshots at once. Then there are a few extra tools like Imagine Combiner to stitch multiple images, Ruler to measure dimensions, Color to extract color values from elements in your screenshots, and more.
Files for File Explorer
File Explorer is Microsoft’s own file manager for Windows. Although it has largely remained unchanged from Windows 10 to Windows 11, it did receive some noteworthy changes in appearance and functionality. Still, some of its elements, like the dialog box, look archaic. Not to mention, it lacks customizability and many features you otherwise find on its alternatives. This is where Files comes in.
Files is a popular File Explorer alternative that gives you everything you get with File Explorer, along with plenty of other useful features, while blending well with Windows 11 aesthetics. For starters, it supports Miller columns, which makes navigating nested folders easier. Likewise, it has a dual-pane mode for side-by-side file and folder comparisons.
Among other things, Files lets you add color-coded tags to files, view folder sizes at a glance, and preview a bunch of different file types like Markdown and SVG natively. It also offers Git integration for developers and a built-in FTP/SFTP client to manage files on remote servers. Last but not least, Files has a Command Palette, which is essentially a search box pop-up where you can search for files, change settings, and perform a bunch of other actions without digging through different menus.
Everything for Windows Search
Windows Search — the built-in search tool on your Windows PC, which lets you find apps, files, settings, and more- has come a long way over the years. It feels more integrated into the system and gives you options to control the kind of results that appear. Still, Search can feel quite slow, especially on relatively older hardware. It actively scans folders in the background, which increases resource usage. For this reason, it’s best to switch to Everything.
Everything is one of the popular file search tools for Windows. Its biggest highlights are speed and low resource usage. This is partly because of the way Everything indexes files and folders. Instead of crawling folders, it reads the NTFS Master File Table (MFT) — a type of database Windows uses to track files on the drive. This also enables Everything to instantly reflect any changes you make to files on your PC.
Among other things, Everything supports Regex and offers granular search options to help you find exactly what you’re looking for. It also has a handy batch renaming tool built in that lets you rename multiple files at once. Everything also has excellent keyboard-based navigation support, if you prefer that. You can even customize your most-used actions to your preferred keyboard shortcuts.
System Informer for Windows Task Manager
im is a powerful Windows app for monitoring and managing apps and background processes running on your computer. It comes in handy when you want to know what (and how much) resources an app or process is using, manage startup apps, and close frozen apps and system processes. However, it doesn’t support advanced task-management operations and isn’t quite effective at many supported tasks. Switching to System Informer thus makes sense.
System Informer provides low-level control over apps and processes, allowing you to manage them more effectively. It uses interactive graphs to show you all the processes hogging system resources. You can click on any data point for more information. This way, you can see all the past and dead processes to find the culprit. Similarly, the app makes it easier to view, start, and stop low-level system drivers, which is useful when you want to fix system crashes.
For times when you see an unknown background process eating up resources, System Informer lets you learn more about it without leaving the app. Last but not least, System Informer lets you find all processes using a particular file and kill them easily. This can be useful when you’re unable to edit or delete a file because some process is using it.
ImageGlass for Microsoft Photos
Microsoft Photos is the app that your PC launches whenever yoscru open a peenso in File Explorer. It lets you view photos and do basic edits (crop, repair, stylize, and enhance). There’s also cloud integration support to help you view and manage photos from your OneDrive or iCloud account right in the app, along with a bunch of AI features. Honestly, though, all of this feels like overkill for an app meant just to view photos. Not only does it make the interface look cluttered, but it also slows the app down significantly. Hence, the need for alternatives like ImageGlass.
ImageGlass is one of the popular Microsoft Photos alternatives after IrfanView. Although IrfanView is packed with advanced features, it feels dated in today’s time. Add to that the fact that Microsoft Photos is primarily a photo viewer, and ImageGlass starts looking like the better option. It’s fast, thanks to its use of hardware caching, which preloads adjacent images so they load instantly when you use the left or right arrow keys. And unlike Photos, it supports over 90 image formats, including WebP, JXL, and multiple RAW formats, natively. As such, you don’t need to download external plugins or extensions to open images.
Another reason to choose ImageGlass is the clean experience. It’s an entirely local-first image viewer that doesn’t integrate cloud services, nor does it push AI or other unrelated features. The app just lets you open images to view them. That said, you do get basic editing options (rotate, flip, crop, resize, etc.), along with a few other useful tools like a color picker and an EXIF metadata viewer. The app’s UI is customizable too, and you get plenty of themes, layouts, and other options to play with.
Those are some Microsoft apps I’ve replaced on my Windows PC with better alternatives. All of them are free to download and use, though some, such as Files and ImageGlass, offer a paid version that unlocks access to a few additional features. You can visit their website to learn more about these features, and if your workflow demands them, upgrade to their paid versions anytime.
