Anime Adventures Update 21 brings several new units and changes to the existing meta, giving players more options for Story, Raids, and Infinity Castle. Some characters stand out through their raw damage, while others offer powerful buffs, crowd control, and passives that can change how an entire team performs. Our Anime Adventures tier list ranks the best units in the Summer Event update so you can decide which characters deserve your resources.
Anime Adventures Units Tier List for Summer Event Update
The best units in Anime Adventures are those that provide consistent damage, useful passives, and strong performance across different game modes. Snow Reaper Final, Elyssa Abyssal, Zombie Risen, and Chuuni Delusion are among the strongest picks, while units such as Captain God and Fused Hero remain valuable for their damage output. It is important to use the resources available from the Anime Adventures codes on the right unit.
Our rankings in the Anime Adventures tier list consider each unit’s damage, range, utility, upgrade requirements, and performance in different modes. S-tier units are the strongest choices, while lower tiers include characters that need specific team setups or have noticeable limitations. So, it is better to use the best Anime Adventures traits with them.

|---|---|

| A | Captain God, Fishi (Obsession), Explosion Mage, Phoenix (Mythic Flames), Spider, Shadow Sorcerer (Ritual), Supreme Being (Sovereign), Switchblade (Deception), Vengeful Swordsman (Sky Reaver), Legendary Assassin (Prime) |

Anime Adventures Tier List for Best Units Explained
A unit’s position on our Anime Adventures tier list depends on more than its damage numbers. Crowd control, damage amplification, air coverage, upgrade costs, and how well its abilities work against bosses all affect its overall value.
Here is a closer look at what each unit brings to your team, along with the situations where you should consider using them.
S-Tier Anime Adventures Units
S-tier units are the strongest choices in Update 21 of Anime Adventures. They offer excellent damage, powerful passives, or support effects that can make the rest of your team considerably stronger.
- Snow Reaper (Final): Snow Reaper slows enemies with her Gale of the Moon ability while dealing damage. Each application adds a Chilled stack, and reaching six stacks freezes the target. Her full AoE hybrid coverage and ability to hit air enemies make her excellent for early defense and difficult waves. She is a strong choice for both beginners and veterans who need reliable crowd control, although her ability uses a fuel system that needs refilling.
- Elyssa (Abyssal): Elyssa is a powerful summoner who calls Abyssal Eels and Jellyfish to deal additional damage. Her Jellyfish explosions deal full AoE Magic damage based on her own damage, while her Wretch Communion passive summons Eels after five takedowns. She can summon up to three Eels, although each lasts only one minute. She is one of the best choices for players who want a summoner with strong independent damage.
- Zombie (Risen): Zombie gains +25% damage and +10% range for every Zombie on the map. Once four Zombies are deployed, every summon on your team receives double damage, making him especially valuable alongside Elyssa and other summoners. His passive also stacks with other buffs, giving summon-focused teams a major advantage. He is worth building for veterans who want to maximize summon damage, but less useful in teams without summoners.
- Chuuni (Delusion): Chuuni increases the Magic damage enemies take by up to 50% per mark, with a maximum of three marks at base. Her Pact of Revelation passive also deals additional damage over time while enemies remain in range. With the Unique trait, her Magic damage amplification can reach a 300% cap. She is a must-have support for Magic-focused teams and a strong investment for players tackling bosses.
- Word Mage: Word Mage permanently curses enemies, reducing their elemental resistance by 10 initially and another 10 every three seconds, up to 80. This makes enemies increasingly vulnerable to your team’s attacks as the fight continues. His resistance reduction makes him an excellent debuffer for longer encounters, especially when paired with powerful DPS units. Prioritize him if you want to improve your entire team’s damage rather than add another standalone attacker.
- Violentine (Brutal Angel): Violentine summons the last enemy she damages at 25% of its original health every five attacks, with a maximum of 10 summons. Her AoE attacks help her generate these summons consistently, giving her a useful role in summon-focused teams. She becomes particularly effective when paired with Zombie, although her upgrade cost makes her less appealing for players who need an inexpensive damage dealer.
A-Tier Anime Adventures Units
A-tier units remain strong choices and can compete with S-tier characters in the right situations. Some offer excellent boss damage or specialized abilities, while others need more investment or a particular team composition to reach their full potential.
- Captain God: Captain God, based on Usopp, is one of the strongest boss killers in Update 21. His Pop Greens artifact allows plants to overgrow, explode for twice their damage, and gain 1.5 times their range. He also deals True Damage and can hit air enemies. He is an excellent investment for Infinity Castle and players who need a powerful early-wave carry, especially after obtaining his artifact.
- Fishi (Obsession): Fishi applies Drowning to enemies with every attack, reducing their sanity by 10% per hit without a stack limit. Once an enemy’s sanity falls below zero, the effect deals a large amount of damage. This makes her particularly useful against bosses with large health pools. She is worth considering for players who need specialized boss damage, although Chuuni offers stronger overall Magic damage support.
- Explosion Mage: Explosion Mage unleashes an explosive attack whenever it becomes available, with its AoE matching her range. Her burst damage is excellent when the explosion connects, but the long recharge time limits her sustained damage. She is a good choice for players who prefer powerful burst attacks, though more consistent DPS units are better for prolonged fights.
- Phoenix (Mythic Flames): Phoenix applies Phoenix Flames to enemies, causing them to take 300% more Burn damage. This makes him an excellent supporting unit for teams built around Burn damage, especially when paired with Spider. His Reincarnation passive also gives the next placement 50% attack after Phoenix is sold at maximum upgrade. He is worth using in Burn-focused teams, but his low drop rate makes him a demanding target for players who do not already have him.
- Spider: Spider deals Burn damage and works particularly well alongside Phoenix. The combination takes advantage of Phoenix’s increased Burn damage effect to improve the team’s damage against affected enemies. He is a specialized pick rather than a universal carry, so prioritize him when you already have the units needed for a Burn-focused team.
- Shadow Sorcerer (Ritual): Shadow Sorcerer applies a 30% Magic damage debuff to enemies, including air targets. At later upgrades, he becomes Hybrid and gains access to his Ritual ability, which sacrifices him to summon Mahoraga. Mahoraga can be tamed three times, allowing you to stack its passives and switch between Defense, Attack, and Boss modes. He is an excellent choice for players who want flexible damage and support, particularly in Magic-focused teams.
- Supreme Being (Sovereign): Supreme Being marks enemies within range for 12 seconds before dealing five times his damage stat to marked targets still in range. He also summons Shade Birth, a companion whose HP equals five times his raw damage and which attacks independently. His AoE attacks and strong range make him useful against groups and bosses. He is a good investment for players who want a powerful unit with additional summon damage, although his setup takes time.
- Switchblade (Deception): Switchblade applies Dismembered to enemies, making them take 20% more damage permanently for the rest of the wave. This effect benefits every other damage dealer on your team, even though Switchblade does not offer the same direct DPS as the top carries. Place him early to let your entire team take advantage of the debuff. He is especially useful for veterans building teams around high-damage units.
- Vengeful Swordsman (Sky Reaver): Vengeful Swordsman deals additional Magic damage equal to his full damage stat with every hit, effectively doubling his base output. His White Flash Draw Technique guarantees a critical hit on the first attack against each enemy and penetrates 60% of both Physical and Magic resistance. Physical damage buffs also improve his Magic damage, making him easier to support. He is an excellent choice for Infinite Mansion and players who want a reliable high-damage carry.
- Legendary Assassin (Prime): Legendary Assassin permanently stacks damage up to 200%, while his range improves through upgrades. This gives him strong scaling during longer waves, although he needs repeated attacks to reach his maximum potential. He is a solid choice for players who can keep enemies within his range long enough to build his passive.
B-Tier Anime Adventures Units
B-tier units are useful in specific situations but generally need more support or careful placement to compete with higher-ranked Anime Adventures characters on our tier list. They can still perform well when their abilities match the requirements of a stage.
- Dark Mage: Dark Mage is a Hybrid unit that works best in the Hill position. He provides coverage against Soaring enemies and can help fill a gap in teams that lack suitable Hill units. He is worth keeping if you need specialized coverage, but stronger damage dealers should take priority when your team already handles those enemies.
- Illusionist: Illusionist is another Hybrid unit that performs better in the Hill position. He offers a way to deal with Soaring enemies, although his overall performance does not match the strongest carries. He is a reasonable option for players who need additional Hill coverage but should not be a priority for veterans with better alternatives.
- Rudo: Rudo has a passive Mana bar that fills automatically. His attacks consume the entire bar to deal additional damage, giving him a straightforward damage mechanic. However, his overall output is not particularly impressive compared with higher-tier options. He is fine for players who need another usable unit but is not worth prioritizing over stronger DPS characters.
- Water Goddess: Water Goddess is a Hill buffer who grants units in her range +50% Water damage. She can also hit Soaring enemies, giving her some additional value in stages with limited Hill coverage. Her main weakness is that her buff only affects Water damage, which restricts her usefulness outside teams built around units such as Elyssa and Fishi. She is worth considering for Water-focused teams, but her limited buff makes her less flexible than other supports.
- Iron Sentinel: Iron Sentinel deploys drones after every 20 takedowns. These drones inherit 25% of his damage, share his range, and remain active for 30 seconds. At Upgrade 6, they inherit 50% of his damage and 120% of his range, attack faster, and last for one minute. He can hit flying enemies at full damage and reach Soaring enemies, making him useful for players who need additional Hill coverage.
- Somber: Somber deals Bleed damage over six ticks and gains circular AoE coverage at higher upgrades. This gives him some value against groups, but other Bleed-focused units offer better performance. He is an option for players who need a Bleed unit early, although veterans should prioritize stronger alternatives.
- Kansai: Kansai can gain up to 200% additional damage after remaining idle for 10 seconds. The problem is that attacking resets the buff, making it difficult to maintain during regular combat. He can work in situations where his passive can be managed, but players looking for consistent damage should choose a more reliable unit.
C-Tier Anime Adventures Units
C-tier units have useful mechanics, but their damage, control effects, or overall performance make them difficult to recommend over stronger alternatives. Keep them if you need to fill a specific role, but avoid spending too many resources on them.
- Troy Flame: Troy Flame charges a Snap Bar with each strike, up to five charges. His next strike then deals an additional 50% damage as True Damage, while hitting a boss fills the bar instantly. However, his attack speed is slower than other options, and the bonus damage does not compete with stronger boss killers. He is suitable for players who lack dedicated boss damage, but should be replaced once better units become available.
- Armored Crusader: Armored Crusader taunts enemies for three seconds with his first hit. Once enemies reach the center of the attack, they are slowed by 20%. His control effect is short, and his damage output is not high enough to justify a regular team slot. Beginners can use him while building their roster, but experienced players should invest in stronger crowd-control units.
Best Anime Adventures Meta Units Tier List
The strongest teams in Anime Adventures need more than one powerful DPS unit. You should combine reliable carries with damage buffers, debuffers, and units that cover Ground, Hill, and Soaring enemies. Here are the standout choices for the current meta, grouped by the role they perform best.
| Category | Best Units | 
|---|---|
| Must-Have DPS & Carries | Fused Hero, Captain God, Elyssa (Abyssal), Snow Reaper (Final), Phoenix (Mythic Flames), Vengeful Swordsman (Sky Reaver), Ghost-kun (Bound), Shinobi (Eternal), Chuuni (Delusion), Supreme Being (Sovereign) | 
| Top Support & Buffers | Word Mage, Griffin (Reincarnation), Water Goddess, Elfy (Sylph), Commander, Wind Dragon, Operator (ROOM), Switchblade (Deception), Bulby | 
| Ground & Hill Standouts | Captain God, Carrot Ultra, Bego Mage 2, Iron Sentinel, Water Goddess, Megumin, Dark Mage, Illusionist | 
Build your team around a reliable DPS carry, then use support units to increase its damage and control enemy movement. A balanced lineup with the right Ground and Hill coverage will generally perform better than a team filled with damage dealers that all serve the same purpose.
That ends our ultimate Anime Adventures tier list for the top units. Which units are you using in your team composition? Let us know in the comments.
What are the best units in Anime Adventures Update 21?
Snow Reaper (Final), Elyssa (Abyssal), Zombie (Risen), Chuuni (Delusion), Word Mage, and Violentine (Brutal Angel) are the best units in Update 21. They offer strong damage, powerful passives, and useful team support.
Which units are best for support in Anime Adventures?
Word Mage, Chuuni (Delusion), Switchblade (Deception), and Water Goddess are among the best support units. They weaken enemies, amplify team damage, or provide specialized buffs to help your carries perform better.
Which units should I prioritize upgrading in Anime Adventures?
Prioritize S-tier units such as Snow Reaper (Final), Elyssa (Abyssal), Zombie (Risen), and Chuuni (Delusion). They perform well across different game modes and provide strong damage or utility.

Railway officer found dead in Agra DRM office; family alleges suicide due to 'toxic' work culture
A 32-year-old railway officer was found dead in his office chamber in Agra. His wife alleged that he faced harassment and long working hours after a transfer.
A 32-year-old railway officer was found dead in one of the chambers at the divisional railway manager's Office in Agra, officials said on Monday.
The deceased, Abhishek Singh Kushwaha, was posted as an assistant operations manager (AOM) in the Agra railway division. His body was found on a sofa in an office chamber at around 11 pm on Sunday, police said.
Kushwaha's wife and mother have alleged that a toxic work culture and mental harassment by a senior official drove him to take his own life.
Sanjay Gautam, PRO, Agra Division, confirmed the incident but dismissed the allegations levelled by the family members.
Also read: Navi Mumbai police officer dies by suicide
"Kushwaha was found lying on a sofa in the chamber of the senior divisional operations manager (general). He was taken to the hospital, where he was declared dead," Gautam said.
"His post-mortem report is yet to come. Since the matter is under police investigation, I cannot say anything further," he added.
When asked about the family's allegations of mental harassment by the senior divisional operations manager (coordination), Gautam dismissed them as "baseless" and declined to share further details.
"These are all baseless allegations," Gautam said.
In a complaint filed with the police, Kushwaha's wife, Astha Rani, stated that on November 1, 2026, her husband had told her that he was going to the office. He later returned home at around 4 pm to collect a diary.
Rani added in her complaint that he appeared very disturbed at the time. When she called him about an hour later, at around 5 pm, he did not respond. Later that night, she learnt about his death.
She said her husband had been transferred from Prayagraj to Agra around three months ago and had allegedly been facing harassment since then.
She alleged that the senior divisional operations manager (coordination) had subjected her husband to a stressful work environment, making him work from 9 am to 11 pm, and had threatened to ruin his career if he did not follow his orders.
The incident has sent shockwaves among other railway staff members, who have demanded strict action against the person responsible.

Railway employees staged a protest outside the divisional railway manager's office, holding senior officials responsible for the officer's death and demanding action against them.
"The toxic work culture at the DRM office has led to Kushwaha's death. We want action against the accused official, and we will continue our protest until justice is delivered," a staff member said.

Graham said during a campaign event in Greenville, South Carolina, on Oct. 28, that "When I get to heaven one day, I am just going to choke Lindsey." The reply was in answer to a question about whether she was angry with her brother as part of the grieving process.
We found no evidence in the Oct. 28 interview or in other reporting that Graham said she did not want to be a senator. Rather, The New York Times reported that said at a campaign event on Oct. 27 that "I actually love the job," speaking about her time in the Senate.
Days before the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, a claim circulated that Darline Graham, the senator from South Carolina who filled the vacancy left by her brother Lindsey Graham's death in July, said she did not want to be a senator and that, "When I get to heaven one day, I am just going to choke Lindsey."
One X post (archived) that shared the purported quote had nearly 1 million views at the time of this writing.
Claims about what Graham allegedly said also circulated on Facebook and Bluesky (archived, archived). Snopes readers contacted us asking about the claim.
The claim was a mixture of true and false elements. It was true that Graham said during a radio interview (at 34:00) on Oct. 28 that, "When I get to heaven one day, I am just going to choke Lindsey."
However, there was no evidence that Graham ever said she did not want to be a senator. She had reportedly said at a campaign event the day before that "I actually love the job," speaking about her time in the Senate. Rather, Graham appeared to be expressing frustration at the timing of her appointment and intense primary election campaign due to her brother's unexpected death when she said she wanted to choke him.
Graham spoke about wanting to choke her brother in response to a question during an interview with the local radio station WYRD-FM. One of the interviewers asked (at 31:35):
We hear that there are stages of grief. One of those is anger. Do you sometimes just say, "Lindsey, what did you do to me?" Do you get a little angry with Lindsey for putting you in this situation?
Graham in response spoke about the process of first agreeing to serve out her brother's term and then to run for a full term in the 2026 elections, the latter at the request of President Donald Trump. Graham said part of the reason she agreed to take over her brother's term and run for her own full term was to carry on his legacy.
On her grief, Graham said (at 34:00):
GRAHAM: Some days hit me harder than other days, especially with the grief. I told somebody one time, I said, you know, "When I get to heaven one day, I am just gonna choke Lindsey …"
INTERVIEWER: There you have it!
GRAHAM: … leaving me like this. But I think he would be proud, I really do. And, like, I will never be able to fill his shoes, but we come from the same background, a humble background with two hardworking parents. So I have that same strong work ethic he had. He worked like a dog. I work myself like a dog, and we care about the people of South Carolina.
We found no evidence during any public appearance by Graham that she ever said outright she did not want to be a senator. Given the prominence of her senatorial race, reputable media outlets would have widely reported such a remark, if true.
Graham's campaign to keep her Senate seat has become emblematic of what Time magazine described as the Republican Party "struggling to maintain voter support" in the 2026 midterms. South Carolina last had a Democratic senator, Ernest F. Hollings, in 2005.
Polling from The New York Times found that voters were equally likely to vote for Graham or her Democratic opponent, Annie Andrews. The Cook Political Report, which provides independent, nonpartisan analysis of elections and campaigns, said the South Carolina senatorial race leaned Republican.

Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a mass atrocity that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days.
A year after the fall of El Fasher, the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city.
A total of 15 commanders from the military groups – the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) – have been subjected to a travel ban and an asset freeze.
The Foreign Office said it hoped the action would ensure “the horrors that took place at El Fasher will be known to the world”.
During the RSF’s takeover of the city, up to 10,000 men, women and children are believed to have been slaughtered over two days – the fastest and largest massacre of civilians this century. Another 40,000 remain unaccounted for.
The killings came at the end of an 18-month starvation siege by the RSF, which was allegedly backed by the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The UAE continues to deny supporting the RSF.
Fewer than 70,000 people are believed to remain in El Fasher, compared with a prewar population of more than 1 million. Life inside the city continues to be horrendous, with testimony indicating routine detention, torture and unlawful killings.
Individuals targeted by the UK’s latest sanctions include Hussein Abu Jalak, an RSF colonel linked to atrocities during the siege, which forced hundreds of thousands of civilians to live off animal feed.
Another is Al-Nour Ahmed Adam – also known as “Al-Qubba” – who was identified as playing a prominent role in the attack on the city.
A Guardian investigation earlier this year revealed internal US and UK warnings were sidelined in the run-up to the RSF attack on El Fasher, and that action that might have saved lives was not taken.
A statement to mark the anniversary of the massacre from the Coalition on Atrocity Prevention and Justice for Sudan said: “The victims will not be forgotten, survivors will be heard, and we will continue to pursue accountability for those responsible.”
During the 12 months since the fall of El Fasher, Sudan’s ruinous conflict – which has forced 14 million people to flee their homes – has developed increasingly into a drone war.
The latest strikes saw the RSF causing mass power outages across east Sudan after targeting power stations with a coordinated drone attack.

There are advantages to all this real estate. The advanced thermal design, with multiple heatsinks and channels for airflow, allows the router to operate at top performance reliably over the long term without a noisy fan. It remained silent and cool to the touch throughout my month of testing. There’s also space for a generous array of ports, including a 10Gbps WAN/LAN, a 10 Gbps LAN, four 2.5Gbps (one WAN/LAN), one 1Gbps LAN, a USB 3.2 Gen1, and a USB 2.0 port. You can even use link aggregation on the two 10 Gbps ports (y’know, just in case you need a 20 Gbps conduit).
Inside, you’ll find Broadcom’s BCM 6718 Wi-Fi chip, featuring a 2.6GHz quad-core processor, 256 MB of Flash memory, and 2 GB of DDR4 RAM. This is a quad-band router, so you have the usual 2.4 and 5 GHz bands, alongside two 6 GHz bands. I don’t want to drown you in spec soup here, but these are all 4 x 4 with OFDMA (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access), 4096-QAM, and maximum-width channels, so we’re talking theoretical top speeds of 1.3 Gbps for the 2.4 GHz band, 5.6 Gbps for the 5 GHz band, and 11.5 Gbps for each of the 6 GHz bands. If you need explanations of the jargon and why each of these specs matter, you’ll find them in my detailed guide to how to buy a router. Just know that this router is at the top of the game.
Further and Faster
Of course, you never get maximum speeds in real life, but the speed of the Asus ROG Rapture GT-BN98 Pro does not disappoint. You can reasonably expect up to 3 Gbps in the same room, around 1 Gbps through a wall, and I was still able to pull 350 Mbps at the bottom of my thick-walled old home’s garden. Comparing my upgrade pick of the best Wi-Fi routers, the tri-band Wi-Fi 7 Asus RT-BE96U, the GT-BN98 Pro proved slightly faster at all distances and longer-range across the board on every band. It also has an extra 6 GHz band, perfect for wireless backhaul if you want to use AiMesh (Asus’s mesh networking functionality) to create a mesh with another Asus router.
Multi-Link Operation (MLO), enabling you to connect devices on multiple bands simultaneously, seems to be maturing since its buggy debut with Wi-Fi 7. It enabled close-range speeds close to 5 Gbps in my tests, but that's using a second Asus ROG Rapture GT-BN98 Pro as a client (most Wi-Fi 8 devices, when they arrive, won't manage that).
Bear in mind that I can’t test the Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC) support yet, which cross-checks with licensed services in the area so your router can boost power for increased range and coverage on the 6 GHz band. It is available in the US and will be in the UK soon, but not every country allows it, and your mileage will vary depending on your local licensees.
Wi-Fi 8 isn’t primarily about higher speeds. It aims to improve stability and reliability with a raft of features that compensate for local interference and reduce latency for important tasks like gaming. The Asus ROG Rapture GT-BN98 Pro boasts adaptive Quality of Experience and device optimization, automatically recognizing gaming devices and streams and giving them priority.

Get better at: Showing leadership potential
Today's move
If you want to get promoted, don't just bring your boss problems — come to them with possible solutions when something goes wrong.
Jason Kidd, the chief operating officer at Chipotle, visits roughly a dozen restaurants every week and he uses team dinners in every location as a way to scout talent for promotions. He said he looks for four qualities in the people he promotes, including how they respond when things go wrong.
Why it works
At any company, including a fast-moving restaurant like Chipotle, problems are bound to arise. Kidd looks for leaders who can anticipate issues, take ownership, and find a solution.
Those employees show they aren't waiting around for problems to land in their lap. They're actively taking initiative to improve the workplace.
Try it today
The next time an issue comes up at work, take a few minutes to brainstorm possible solutions.
When you approach your manager, tell them what went wrong, a couple of possible solutions, and your recommendation for what to do next. That demonstrates leadership and initiative.
The bottom line
You aren't directly responsible for every problem that comes up at work. However, by showing your boss that you're actively working to avoid adding another task to their to-do list, you're helping make their job easier and showing them that you can handle more responsibility.
Source
This insight is based on Business Insider's reporting about how Chipotle's COO Jason Kidd promotes workers, and the qualities he looks for. Read the full story from Ana Altchek on Business Insider.

Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
- Published
Kenya is grappling with its first ever outbreak of Ebola, a disease which neighbouring countries, such as Uganda and Democratic Republic of Congo, are used to dealing with.
Nine cases have now been confirmed including its first patient, who travelled from DR Congo and died two weeks ago.
Four relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner have now tested positive, meaning they are all linked to him.
But concerns are rising that the virus could start spreading further, even as the government has sought to assure citizens.
The US has warned it citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert.
Should Kenyans be concerned?
Kenyans have been expressing their concerns that the disease could spread more widely.
More than 4,000 people have died since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease.
With more than 9,500 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according to the International Rescue Committee, which has been working alongside both governments to contain the spread.
The latest outbreak has been caused by the Bundibugyo species, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.
Kenyans raised questions from the outset, about how the first patient was able to spend time in the region worst-affected by Ebola, then travel to two more countries before his illness was identified. He died days after his arrival in Kenya.
As a regional transport hub, the risk of the outbreak spreading is a big concern.
The doctors' union in Kenya has expressed concerns at "lapses" at various border points, including with neighbouring Uganda and Tanzania, as well as at Kenya's main airport.
Dennis Miskellah, the union representative, told the BBC that border and port facilities were grossly understaffed.
However, Health Director-General Patrick Amoth on Tuesday evening sought to reassure people, saying that the eight patients were all improving and responding well to treatment.
What is being done to stop it spreading?
When the first case was announced, the authorities urged people not to panic, assuring them of heightened surveillance at airports and border crossings.
Kenya has since introduced enhanced screening for travellers arriving from 10 countries it considers to be at high risk: DR Congo, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Angola, Zambia, Ethiopia, South Sudan and the Central African Republic.
Travellers arriving from those countries are required to complete a digital surveillance form before boarding their flights, and to present a QR code to port health officials on arrival.
Kenya also ordered enhanced public health screening of aircraft arriving from those countries, as authorities seek to prevent further imported cases.
Within the country, the government has been sharing public messages to create awareness about Ebola, including encouraging people to promptly report any suspected cases and seek care at a hospital.
It has also focused on hygiene and safety measures, such as washing hands and avoiding close contact with sick people.
The government has additionally designated treatment and isolation facilities across the country, and health workers have been trained to deal with the disease.
Amoth also said that a dedicated laboratory had been set up at the Kenyatta National Hospital Infectious Disease Unit to handle Ebola tests, to ensure that the hospital's laboratory was not contaminated.
In Kenya, 134 out of 135 people listed as contacts of the first patient remain in quarantine. That means about 99% of the contacts have been traced and isolated, in order to prevent Ebola from spreading to the wider population.
That all of those infected so far had links to the first victim shows Kenya's early response is working, according to the International Rescue Committee.
The government is also working with international partners, including Africa CDC and the World Health Organization (WHO), to support its response, including surveillance, communication and community engagement.
A toll-free emergency hotline, 719, has been provided to the public to report suspected symptoms.
Is Kenya prepared in case it starts spreading further?
Amoth said that none of the contacts of the first patients had showed symptoms before going into quarantine "and therefore the potential to spread to another person is very minimal, literally non-existent".
The incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks. The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.
Despite that, Kenya's health ministry says nearly 5,000 healthcare workers have been trained to deal with Ebola at the national and local levels, besides the facilities that have been designated to handle the virus.
The ministry has urged people to remain calm and vigilant. It has also asked Kenyans not to stigmatise people identified as contacts of Ebola cases.
The ministry, along with the WHO, have produced posters to help people understand Ebola and support its containment. One message reads: "Stop stigma, choose support. Stigma can discourage people from reporting symptoms or cooperating with response teams."
In addition, the government has procured supplies of protective equipment.
Is enough being done to protect health workers?
Not according to the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Union (KMPDU).
With three health workers and a hospital cleaner among those infected, questions have been asked as to whether the government could do more to protect workers.
Health workers and carers can face a higher risk of Ebola infection because caring for infected patients may bring them into contact with blood and other bodily fluids.
- What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult? 
  - Published15 September
Dennis Miskellah, the KMPDU deputy secretary general, told the BBC that protective equipment must be provided to hospitals so that they are fully protected, especially in case patients with symptoms do not declare that they have been in areas with Ebola.
He suggests the government ought to conduct proper health education to destigmatise the virus, so that people do not seek to hide their symptoms.
The International Rescue Committee has also called for continued funding for contact tracing, border screening and training of frontline health workers in Kenya.
Will there be any restrictions, like a travel ban?
Kenya remains open with no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings.
Despite confirming the eight cases, the authorities have explicitly ruled out a national lockdown or general travel ban for Kenyans.
The US on Monday issued an advisory asking citizens to reconsider travelling to the country over Ebola concerns. Other countries have issued health alerts, including the UK, which warned its citizens that they may encounter enhanced health screening, and Canada, which has asked citizens to monitor their health for 21 days.
No country has issued an outright ban against their nationals visiting Kenya, nor have Kenyans been blocked from entering other countries over Ebola fears.
Has business and tourism been affected?
Analysts have raised concerns over the potential impact of public health fears on international travel and tourism but there is no evidence this has happened yet.
But the situation could change if the outbreak were to spread into the wider population.
How many Kenyans are there in DR Congo?
The exact number of Kenyans living in the DR Congo is not clear.
A report authored last year by the Centre for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) think-tank put the number of Kenyans living in eastern DR Congo at about 2,500, including about 50 investors. It also noted that there were about four times as many Congolese living in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, alone.
The Kenyan embassy in the Congolese capital, Kinshasa, which represents Kenya's interests in four countries - DR Congo, Central African Republic, Congo-Brazzaville and Gabon - has in the past urged Kenyans living in the region to formally register so that it is able to serve them better.
How have neighbouring countries responded?
Several countries in the region have announced tightening of surveillance measures and enhanced screening for visitors.
One man who came into contact with the man who died in Kenya is under quarantine in Somalia and samples have been sent to Kenya for testing.
Somalia has also said it was taking precautionary measures, including enhancing surveillance measures at border points "given the evolving regional situation and the movement of people between countries".
The suspected case in Somalia had travelled through Ethiopia, which has also said it had tightened surveillance to prevent an outbreak
In Tanzania, visitors are expected to undergo daily health monitoring for 21 days, through an automated tracking system, which was announced after Kenya confirmed multiple cases of Ebola infections.
Uganda said after Kenya's first Ebola case that it was continuing to "maintain strong surveillance measures to protect public health".
The Kenyan businessman had travelled through Uganda on his way home from DR Congo.
Uganda had reported two Ebola deaths shortly after the outbreak was reported in DR Congo, but the WHO has since declared it to be free of the disease.
On Tuesday, Nigeria confirmed a case of Ebola in a female patient who travelled from Uganda to Abuja. Nigeria is the first West African state to report a case linked to the current Ebola crisis in East and Central Africa.
Ugandan health officials say the woman had travelled to eastern DR Congo for business before passing through Uganda in early October.
The health ministry stressed she did not have symptoms while transiting through Uganda and only developed them after arriving in Abuja.

24 hours in Antigua: Mark Carney's priorities at this year's Commonwealth Summit
While Americans vote on their future, Canada’s PM locks in on alternative partnerships
Prime Minister Mark Carney's oft-stated determination to keep his government focused on what Canadians can control could be tested today, as he meets with leaders from the 55 other member countries of the Commonwealth in Antigua.
As he boarded his flight with his wife Diana on Monday, Carney gestured as if he couldn't hear reporters yelling for clarification on where things stand following his conversation with U.S. President Donald Trump over the weekend.
Trade negotiations could return to a full boil, but for now they remain on a back burner while the White House focuses on the verdict about to be rendered by American voters in their midterm elections.
The future of the Canada-U.S. relationship hangs so heavy over the Carney government's agenda that it could be hard to focus on anything else. But this week's Commonwealth talks are the first in a series of multilateral summits this month where Canadian officials will pursue alternative partnerships in trade, security and diplomacy.
Here are five things to watch for:
1. Push to double intra-Commonwealth trade
The Commonwealth has three main priorities leading up to 2030: democratic resilience, economic resilience and environmental resilience.
On that first priority, ministers, including Foreign Minister Anita Anand, met Sunday to welcome the restoration of an elected government in Gabon, the central African country which had its membership partially suspended following a military coup in 2023.
But the main focus at this summit is trade partnerships: specifically the association's ambition to lower trade barriers and double trade between member countries by the time they meet for their next biennial summit.
That dovetails perfectly with the Carney government's attempt to pivot away from the U.S.
- Canada's next budget to be unveiled this week amid U.S. trade war, economic uncertainty
- Experts suggest Canada lock in gains with EU amid 'associate member' confusion
"I think people don't realize the economic clout of the Commonwealth. There's almost a trillion dollars of trade," said Arif Lalani, a former diplomat who served as a senior official the last time a Canadian prime minister attended the Commonwealth Summit, in 2022.
"There are studies which show that it's cheaper to do business between Commonwealth countries because we have the same practices, same language, generally the same set of regulations. So it's definitely a place to pursue the economic diversification agenda," Lalani said.
His fear, however, is that the Commonwealth's "relevance is growing faster than its capacity to deliver."
Leaders need to get more outcome-oriented on trade, he said. He agrees with Carney's efforts to expand this focus to defence and security co-operation too.
At a time when conflicts over choke points like the Strait of Hormuz are restricting global trade, "Commonwealth countries have a lot of coastline, they have strong navies, and so I think there's something that can be done to increase maritime co-operation," Lalani said.
2. Evolving Caribbean relationships
This is Carney's first trip to the Caribbean as prime minister.
That diplomatic deficiency will be addressed this morning in a bilateral meeting with this year's Commonwealth host, Antigua and Barbuda's Prime Minister Gaston Browne, followed by a working breakfast Canada is hosting for all the Caribbean leaders attending this year's summit.
While not a complete gathering of CARICOM leaders, officials briefed reporters that this breakfast is a chance to discuss trade and investment, climate action and regional security.
Prime Minister Mark Carney and Diana Fox Carney are met by a greeting party as they arrive in Antigua. (Christopher Katsarov/The Canadian Press)
Vandana Kattar, who worked in the prime minister's office under former prime minister Justin Trudeau, says Carney's approach so far makes sense to her.
"Multilateralism is important to him," she said. Carney went after some of the bigger pieces of his puzzle first, she reckons — pursuing the "low-hanging fruit" of a closer relationship with Europe, attempting to resolve tariff tensions with China.
"Those are big pieces of the puzzle that he's been able to put together," she said. But he also needs to fit smaller pieces into that puzzle, like nurturing Canada's relationships in the Caribbean, "otherwise that doesn't complete the whole picture."
3. Climate finance commitments
"You can't go to the Caribbean countries and not talk of climate resiliency," Kattar said. "They're the ones impacted the most."
Canada's already contributed $4.65 million over three years to the Commonwealth's climate finance access hub to help small island states. It's also made a bigger $13-billion commitment to support all developing countries adapt to the consequences of climate change — like stronger and more frequent hurricanes — over the next five years.
- Netherlands must cut CO2 to protect Caribbean island of Bonaire, court rules
- Video Small island nations want largest emitters to pay for catastrophic effects of climate change
Canada hopes to amplify the voices of smaller Commonwealth partners on climate issues, officials told reporters prior to the trip.
"That's what actually builds the trust, and that's what ensures that Canada is seen as a reliable and a trustworthy partner that actually listens to the concerns of their partners and [is] not just forcing their own agenda onto them," said Climate Action Network's Soomin Han.
Han believes conversations on climate financing between big and small Commonwealth partners might be more productive than at United Nations climate conferences, where a few large countries can block progress.
"Countries should not have to take out more debt simply to survive a crisis they contributed comparatively little to creating," she said.
4. Tensions, debate on reparations
While the Commonwealth has 56 members, King Charles is the head of state in only 15 of them. Half of those are Caribbean countries, and for the week leading up to this summit, he's been touring the region, amid ongoing political pressure for the Crown and the government of the United Kingdom to apologize for its historical role profiting off the slave trade in British colonies.
So far, the King has acknowledged "the great suffering and injustices of the past in these islands and beyond," but he has not apologized.
Canadian officials briefing reporters prior to the trip said Canada acknowledges the generational and lasting impact of slavery, and supports "open and respectful dialogue" on reparations, but noted there are a "diversity" of perspectives on reparatory justice among Commonwealth members.
Nicholas Marcus Thompson, an advocate for reparations for Canada's Black communities, says the current U.K. government's opposition to negotiating reparations for slavery is "simply a non-starter" for Caribbean nations.
"Reparations is not giving away a freebie. It's repaying what you took, right? Wealth extracted from enslaved Africans built businesses, financial institutions, universities," said Thompson, who is also the president and CEO of the Black Class Action Secretariat.
"It would have been billions of dollars in today's currency."
5. The Trump factor
Former diplomat Lalani said he believes Canada is heading into this summit with more credibility than it's had in the past, thanks to the "provocative vision" Carney laid out in his speech on middle powers at the World Economic Forum in Davos last winter.
Carney's conversations today won't be limited to people he's close to, like Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. It's also a chance to talk to leaders with whom he doesn't have full agreement — without being overshadowed by superpowers like the U.S. or China.
"Canada can have a discussion with other countries without the baggage of having the United States at the table," he said.
"The biggest destabilizing power in the world right now is the United States. … That requires a candid discussion."

Do screens in cars represent luxury? Judging by the latest car interiors, the answer would seem to be an emphatic “yes.” Screens aren’t just getting larger; they are multiplying across the dashboard and morphing into different forms and concepts. Indeed, an interior’s screens are a pretty good indicator of what brand made the car—or at least how much the owner paid for it.
But is this actually what customers want? Are more screens really better? And even if they are, luxury car features inevitably trickle down to cheaper, more mainstream offerings, and screens can only get so big. That leaves luxury automakers with another question to answer: “What’s next?”
Mercedes-Benz is working on a new display alternative that could provide an answer. For now, it’s known as the holographic display. Forget the images from Star Trek and Star Wars that just popped into your head, though. It’s effectively a more advanced form of heads-up display, or HUD.
Eyes on the road, not the dash
Whereas a traditional HUD projects images onto the windshield glass, the holographic display has two main components. It still uses a projector, but its key element is a special transparent film laminated into the glass. The film uses holographic optical elements, or “super-small mirrors,” as Mercedes development engineer Lena Hees described them, that selectively reflect the light emitted by the projector, keeping the image visible even in direct sunlight while hiding it from the driver’s view.
Today, the passenger-side touchscreens in Mercedes and other luxury vehicles rely on driver-monitoring cameras or screen polarization to keep the driver from seeing what is playing on the passenger side.
Speaking of passenger screens, the holographic display is clearly being considered as a future alternative or replacement for this technology. Although screens in cars are increasingly ubiquitous, a recent JD Power study indicated that car owners classify passenger screens as “not necessary” and have generally negative opinions about them. Mercedes has clearly observed similar opinions but for slightly different reasons.
“We have customers who like the Hyperscreen,” said development engineer Maximilian Hilger of the pillar-to-pillar screen found in an increasing number of Mercedes models. “But there are others who want to maintain luxury materials.”
In other words, the massive screen design doesn’t seem as luxurious as the pillar-to-pillar bands of wood or other materials found in previous-generation models. And that’s not an opinion isolated to Mercedes’ customers.
New Mercedes chief design officer Bastian Baudy recently told German magazine Auto Motor Sport that “Materiality and haptics must remain tangible—with switches, buttons, and intuitive controls. Real materials are at the heart of Mercedes: metal, wood.”
Mercedes CEO Ola Källenius went further, grouping interior quality and materials among the brand’s “forever values,” along with safety and maintaining what a Mercedes is like to drive.
That presents conflicting priorities, however.
“Yes, you need to have all the [technology] that a customer could ever dream of and wants,” Källenius told Ars. “But you need to package it in an aesthetically pleasing way. That’s also part of it.”
That brings us back to the holographic display. Keep in mind that the photos in this article show early prototypes I saw at Mercedes’ research facilities in Sindelfingen, Germany. The prototype projector sits inside a rather crude, trapezoidal hole dug into the dash of a right-hand-drive, pre-2027 S-Class. It’s also loud, with a cooling fan whirring like a laptop visiting too many junk-filled websites.
The production version would have a much smaller projector opening than those of the prototype and existing heads-up displays. Manual Holstein, a manager working in Mercedes research for future displays, indicated that the projector could be small enough to be hidden behind wood or metal trim pieces. Holstein also said you won’t hear a fan in the production model and that the resolution would improve.
The resolution is certainly considerably better than any current head-up display, including Mercedes’ own, which features augmented reality elements. Full-color, commercial-like videos of the C-Class Electric played during the demonstration, and the display was sufficiently bright, even though Holstein said the prototype was operating at just 20 percent of its maximum brightness.
It’s not there yet
Issues remain, however. The resolution may be good compared to the arrows, script, and graphics of a current HUD, but it’s poor when compared to a passenger touchscreen. The video’s contrast was also too high, and as you can see in the photos, the picture was distorted into a narrow height due to the angle of the windshield. Frankly, no one would choose to watch anything on it over a phone, tablet, or conventional passenger screen. It needs to improve by orders of magnitude before becoming a viable alternative.
Again, though, this is just a prototype. Holstein said the holographic film size, or “eyebox,” can be made much bigger and be raised higher than the HUD-like height of the prototype. He also dismissed the distortion as a problem unique to the prototype.
Imagine nearly half the windshield transformed into a virtual screen that’s visible only to the passenger. Beyond videos or other entertainment, Mercedes envisions the holographic display highlighting points of interest in the view through the windshield. A similar display could be placed on the driver side, showing situational information, enabling video calls, or providing entertainment when parked. In the future, it could even let drivers watch things other than the road when Mercedes’ Level 3 autonomous driving system allows them to take their eyes off it. At the very least, the technology could replace today’s HUDs and their larger projector boxes.
Currently, it might work for a weather widget, but you won’t want to watch a video.
Credit:
Mercedes-Benz
Currently, it might work for a weather widget, but you won’t want to watch a video.
Credit:
Mercedes-Benz
Having experienced the prototype while the car was moving, I also think the holographic display could help prevent the motion sickness that can come from staring at a passenger screen while the car is moving. The higher screen angle and ability to see more of the outside world beyond created a notably different visual experience.
Of course, the question remains: “Is this what customers want?”
If the JD Power survey found that customers don’t care about passenger touchscreens, will they be any more enthusiastic about holographic video displays? That seems doubtful. But that’s just as much of an open question as whether the production version will actually live up to its promises.
There’s also another matter: What, exactly, defines luxury? Before Bastian Baudy took over as Mercedes’ chief design officer this year, his predecessor and former boss Gordon Wagener echoed Källenius’ thoughts about the direction of the brand’s interiors. He was considerably blunter, though.
“Screens are not luxury,” Wagener told ABC News. “You have a better—and bigger—TV at home, right? And every car has a big screen. So we have to create luxury beyond the screen. That’s why I talk about craftsmanship and sophistication.”
If the holographic display lets automakers emphasize traditional design and materials while still offering unique technology, it could be a promising way forward.

Beijing’s annual independent queer film festival has been cancelled after what is understood to have been a campaign of sustained harassment from authorities.
Beijing Queer film festival, which was due to begin on Friday in China’s capital, is one of the country’s oldest independent film festivals.
In a statement posted on Instagram late on Thursday, the organisers said: “We regret to inform you that the Love Queer Film Week … has been cancelled. We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience and disappointment that the cancellation of this event may cause to those who planned to participate or had been looking forward to the film week.”
Police had increased pressure on the festival through repeated phone calls in recent weeks, it is understood.
Founded in 2001 by a group of Peking University students, the festival grew to become the only film festival in mainland China to offer a public forum for films and discussions exploring LGBTQ+ issues.
The Chinese authorities have grown increasingly intolerant of open discussion of feminist or LGBTQ+ issues. Film festivals in particular attract particular scrutiny because they provide an opportunity to platform narratives that sit outside the Communist party’s worldview.
Beijing Independent film festival, China’s most prominent independent film festival, was closed down in 2014 after the authorities detained the founders and shut off the electricity supply to the venue. Last year, an independent Chinese film festival that was due to be held in New York was cancelled after harassment from the Chinese authorities, an incident which raised concern about transnational repression.
Maya Wang, the deputy Asia director for Human Rights Watch, said: “The Chinese government under Xi has been relentlessly tightening social and ideological control, and so any activities outside of those sanctioned by the party-state are subjected to intensifying scrutiny and often also official harassment.
“The authorities have put more pressure on what little is left of China’s civil society, as well as the LGBT communities and independent film-makers. A queer film festival basically faces all of these overlapping pressures.”
Hongwei Bao, a professor of Chinese studies at the University of St Andrews who focuses on LGBT issues, said that the festival was “a beacon for LGBT resilience” in China.
“The shutdown of the Love Queer Cinema Week has a chilling affect on the Chinese queer community,” Bao said.
In June this year, screenings of films with LGBTQ+ themes that were scheduled to be held in Beijing during Pride month at the Institut Français, a French cultural centre, were cancelled because of police harassment.
Despite the increased pressure, Beijing Queer film festival remains a popular event. Several international film-makers whose work had been selected for the festival had travelled to China to participate. Last year, the festival received 200 volunteer applications, four times the number received in 2024.
Beijing’s public security bureau could not be reached for comment.

October was a month of contrasts for the Indian startup ecosystem. While AI, deeptech and advanced manufacturing continued to attract significant investor capital, a series of cybersecurity incidents and regulatory actions highlighted the risks and responsibilities that come with scaling digital businesses. The month saw India’s cybersecurity watchdog CERT-In flag unauthorised access to Indian organisations’ live systems by AI agents under evaluation, alongside the use of agentic tools in financially motivated cyberattacks. Digital trust company eMudhra faced a major security setback after researchers recovered eight weak private keys from publicly available certificates, prompting Google, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft to distrust the affected certificates. Meanwhile, IRDAI’s proposed insurance commission caps raised concerns among distributors and brokers, with industry representatives warning of significant revenue and employment implications. Together, these developments underscored the mounting compliance, data security and governance challenges confronting India's digital businesses. Amid this, venture capital interest in the ecosystem took a slight hit. Indian startups raised over $686 Mn across 104 funding deals in October, down almost 10% MoM from September's $760.7 Mn. AI remained a major funding theme, while capital also flowed into spacetech, defence, semiconductors and industrial automation. The public markets remained active, with four new-age tech companies making their debuts during the month. Zetwerk, Tonbo Imaging, Moneyview and Snapdeal parent AceVector made their market debuts, while Cult.fit and Atomberg received SEBI's approval for their respective IPOs. Against this backdrop of funding momentum, public-market activity and growing regulatory scrutiny, Inc42 is back with the latest edition of its flagship ‘30 Startups To Watch’ series, spotlighting early-stage ventures that stood out to us in October. The cohort spans innovation in deeptech, automation and consumer tech, from AI evaluation platforms and autonomous systems to lunar infrastructure, advanced imaging sensors and new-age consumer brands. With that said, here are the 30 startups that made the cut last month. _________________________________________________________________ The 1970 Shop | A Cleaner Label For India’s Traditional Snacks Diwali and mindful eating rarely go hand in hand. Between boxes of mithai and endless servings of namkeen, even the most disciplined eaters find it difficult to resist. While traditional snacks remain irresistible, many are made using refined flour, saturated oil, white sugar and other ingredients that health-conscious consumers increasingly seek to avoid. Delhi-based The 1970 Shop is looking to offer an alternative with traditional Indian snacks made without added preservatives or acidity regulators. Founded in July 2025 by Lalit, Manju and Vipul Mittal, along with Puruvi Poddar, the startup makes its products in-house, including flour milled using wheat, chana dal, ragi and jowar. Its portfolio includes atta biscuits, thekua, dal kachori papdi and besan laddoos, made using ingredients such as desi ghee, groundnut oil, jaggery and desi khaand. Selling through its website, Amazon and other channels, The 1970 Shop claims to have served over 50,000 customers. The startup says it has more than doubled revenue over three months and achieved CM2 profitability. It is targeting an FY27 revenue run rate of ₹18 Cr and plans to increase monthly sales from 30 tonnes to 150 tonnes by 2028. _________________________________________________________________ Archgen Labs | Using AI To Make Chip Design Efficient As demand for AI computing pushes chipmakers towards increasingly complex semiconductor architectures, designing and testing these chips is becoming more challenging. Three-dimensional (3D) chip stacking, which places multiple layers of computing components vertically to improve performance and reduce data-transfer delays, introduces additional engineering challenges, particularly around heat management, placement and timing. This is where San Francisco-based Archgen Labs sees an opportunity. Founded in 2026 by Hariharan Ayappane and Naveen Venkat, Archgen Labs is developing AI-powered electronic design automation (EDA) tools for semiconductor engineers. Its flagship product, Newton, is an AI chip-design engineer that automates backend physical design tasks, including placement, routing, design-rule fixes and timing closure. Its LayerTherm tool analyses chip temperatures and claims to run around 5,000 times faster than conventional simulations in the company's benchmarks. The opportunity is expanding alongside the semiconductor industry. Operating in the global EDA market, projected to reach $24.07 Bn by 2030, the startup's challenge will be integrating its tools into established engineering workflows and proving that its AI systems can reliably handle production-grade chip designs. ________________________________________________________________________ Balisto Agritech | Taking Electric Farm Machines To India’s Small Farmers From preparing land to removing weeds, farming requires different machines for different tasks. For farmers, this means higher equipment costs, fuel expenses and dependence on manual labour. Mumbai-based Balisto Agritech wants to simplify farm operations with a multipurpose electric machine that can perform several tasks. Founded in 2024 by Aishwarya Ramakrishnan and Kedar Gokhale, the startup has developed Balisto 130 Pro, a 13 hp electric power tiller designed for land preparation, weeding, inter-cultivation, puddling and earthing up. Powered by detachable batteries and three motors, the machine, priced between ₹2.5 Lakh and ₹3 Lakh, can be operated onboard or remotely. Its IoT connectivity enables machine monitoring and fault diagnosis. Balisto is also developing an autonomous version using GPS and sensors. The startup claims to have sold over 30 machines, covering more than 600 acres of farmland, and generated cumulative sales exceeding ₹60 Lakh since June 2025. With India's agricultural machinery market projected to reach ₹2.72 Lakh Cr by 2034, according to IMARC Group, Balisto is betting on demand for affordable, multipurpose farm equipment. ________________________________________________________________________ CosmoChute | Building The Foundation For Lunar Exploration Popular discourse will have you believe that humanity is just a few years away from inhabiting the moon, with lunar deeds being sold online for ₹1,800 to ₹3,100 per acre. In reality, the infrastructure to colonise the moon is severely lacking and transporting specialised equipment and operating payloads on its surface remain expensive challenges. CosmoChute is betting that these services can be turned into reusable infrastructure that multiple customers can share. Founded in 2026 by rocket engineers Janhavi Gore, Amit Chowdhary and Dhruv Sangal, Ahmedabad-based Cosmochute is developing LEAP, a lunar mobility programme built around three systems: EPOC, a modular rover; OASYS, a payload-carrying trailer; and Cartridge, a system designed to protect payloads from extreme lunar temperatures. The rover will remain on the Moon, transporting new payloads delivered through subsequent missions, while the other systems help carry, power and protect customer experiments. Operating in the lunar rover and mobility vehicle market projected to reach $4.1 Bn by 2032, the startup believes that reusable planetary robotics can lower operating costs for lunar missions. Still in its early stages, Cosmochute plans to test development models in early 2027 and work towards flight qualification by 2028. ________________________________________________________________________ CureMeAbroad | Simplifying Cross-Border Healthcare With AI Medical tourism may not be as glamorous, but it is a booming industry. With patients increasingly travelling abroad for affordable treatment and shorter waiting times, the global market is projected to reach $286.1 Bn by 2030, with India accounting for $16.2 Bn, according to Fortune Business Insights. However, navigating hospitals, treatment plans, travel arrangements and multiple agents can make seeking healthcare abroad a complicated affair. Pune-based CureMeAbroad is looking to simplify this process through an AI-powered platform that helps patients discover and compare hospitals, obtain personalised treatment estimates and book consultations. Founded in 2025 by Aditya Oza and Mikhail Bohra, the startup was inspired by their experience watching a pregnant family member struggle to navigate healthcare arrangements in North America. Beyond hospital discovery, CureMeAbroad assists patients with clinical screening, visas, flights, accommodation and post-treatment follow-ups. The startup claims to work with more than 400 hospital partners across nine treatment destinations and serve around 24,000 patients monthly. While its platform is free for patients, CureMeAbroad earns commissions from partner hospitals and margins on treatment packages. _________________________________________________________________ Cute Brains | Assistive Tech To Bridge Learning Gaps In Kids Up to 15% of children worldwide struggle with learning disabilities like dyslexia and dysgraphia, making activities like reading, writing and spelling much more difficult. These issues often go unidentified in mainstream classrooms in India due to limited awareness and access to specialised assessment and learning support. Delhi NCR-based Cute Brains is using technology to identify and support children with specific learning disabilities (SLD). Founded in 2022 by Braj Bhushan, Manas Sinha and Gyan Prakash, Cute Brains is an IIT Kanpur-incubated startup working across behavioural and cognitive assessment, SLD screening and assistive learning tools. Its flagship product, the Assistive Application for Children with Dyslexia and Dysgraphia, is designed for schoolchildren in classes 1 to 5. The touchscreen-based application combines visual and auditory feedback with haptic sensations and motor movements to help children learn and reproduce letters and words through tracing, puzzles and writing exercises. The startup has already conducted pilots in partnership with government-run schools, and is planning for a commercial launch soon. It offers both individual subscriptions and bundled school services, which include teacher training and preliminary assessments. Beyond its application, Cute Brains conducts awareness programmes, supports non-clinical school-based assessments and works with parents and teachers. It operates in India’s special needs education market, projected to hit $5 Bn by 2030. ________________________________________________________________________ dubdub | Turning The Endless Scroll Into A Game Scrolling through endless videos and social media posts has become second nature for smartphone users. But what if the next swipe brought a puzzle to solve or a trivia question to answer instead? Bengaluru-based dubdub is betting that users will spend more time participating in content rather than simply watching it. Founded in 2026 by Kaustubh Priye and Supan Shah, the startup offers bite-sized trivia, puzzles and mini-games through a swipe-based mobile app. Users can explore over 20 categories, including cricket, Bollywood, mythology and general knowledge. AI-powered personalisation tailors challenges to individual interests, while social features allow users to compete with friends and compare scores. Dubdub claims to have crossed 20,000 downloads. The startup is entering an Indian gaming market projected to grow from $1.5 Bn in 2025 to $3.2 Bn by 2030. However, in a crowded entertainment market, dubdub's challenge will be turning initial downloads into sustained engagement and finding a viable monetisation model. ________________________________________________________________________ Foundry | Rethinking India’s Premium Home Appliance Market India’s home appliance market is crowded with established brands, but much of the competition still revolves around improving existing product categories through incremental upgrades. His entry into the Indian household appliances market comes at a time when it is projected to reach $33.63 Bn by 2030. Foundry is targeting the premium end of this market, where consumers are increasingly looking for differentiated products and technology-led experiences. In October 2026, Foundry raised ₹12 Cr. It plans to use the funds for technology development and product engineering. It will compete with new-age brands like Nush, Atomberg and Nester & Optimist, among others. ________________________________________________________________________ Karta | AI Agents For Voice, Chat And WhatsApp For banks and financial institutions, customer service calls rarely end with answering a question. Bengaluru-based Karta AI is building voice agents to automate these complex interactions. Founded in 2024 by Vijaypal Singh and Abhishek Kushwaha, Karta offers an omnichannel customer communication platform spanning voice, chat, email and WhatsApp. Its agents use a predictive context engine to understand customer intent, draw on institutional policies and previous interactions, and execute workflows across enterprise systems. The startup claims to handle around 2 Mn customer conversations monthly across 25+ languages, with 10–12 paying customers, including PhonePe, Pine Labs, Bajaj and Aavas. Its agents resolve about 70% of borrower queries end-to-end, reducing the cost per query by nearly 50%, according to the company. The startup is building its products in India's conversational AI market, estimated to grow to $3.7 Bn by 2033. ________________________________________________________________________ Lorazzo | Bringing Design To Everyday Bathrooms And Kitchens As Indian homes become increasingly Pinterest-inspired, kitchens and bathrooms are getting their share of the makeover. Yet, consumers still largely depend on contractors and offline retailers offering conventional fittings that prioritise utility and affordability over design. Founded in 2024 by Jatin Luthra and Saurabh Gupta, the startup offers faucets, kitchen sinks, designer basins, sanitaryware and personal-hygiene products. Its portfolio includes Reflekt mirror cabinets, WOGO portable bidets and Lustr stainless steel sinks. It operates in India's bathroom and kitchen fittings market, projected to reach ₹48,300 Cr by FY29. Lorazzo sells through its website and online marketplaces while building an offline network of distributors, retailers and experience centres. Its recently launched sanitaryware range contributes 35% of revenue. Having raised ₹15 Cr in a Sauce.vc-led round, Lorazzo plans to expand its portfolio and distribution network, targeting a ₹25 Cr revenue run rate in FY27. _________________________________________________________________ Lumov Health | Building An Indian Brand For Orthopaedic Recovery Leaving the hospital doesn't always mean the end of treatment. Yet, finding the right support can mean choosing between inexpensive generic products and costly imported alternatives. Bengaluru-based Lumov Health wants to bridge this gap with orthopaedic support designed for Indian consumers. Founded in 2024 by Saumaric Dangwal and Ankit Gupta, the startup designs and manufactures products for post-surgical recovery, rehabilitation and everyday pain management. Its portfolio includes knee and wrist braces, lumbar belts, compression stockings, insoles and hot-and-cold therapy products. Lumov works with orthopaedic specialists and physiotherapists to develop products suited to Indian anatomy and weather conditions. Its products have been developed in collaboration with specialists associated with hospitals such as Manipal, Apollo, Sakra and AIG. The startup is targeting an Indian orthopaedic support market projected to reach $376.2 Mn by 2034. However, with established brands such as Tynor, Flamingo and Vissco already competing for customers, Lumov will need to build trust among doctors and patients to stand out. ________________________________________________________________________ LW3 | Digital Passports For EV Batteries An electric vehicle battery's journey doesn't end when it leaves the factory. From sourcing raw materials to recycling, tracking its lifecycle is becoming increasingly important for manufacturers, regulators and recyclers. Guwahati-based LW3 wants to make this journey traceable through Digital Product Passports (DPPs), which maintain verifiable records of a product's lifecycle. Founded in 2022 by Abhijit Pegu and Marungsha Swrang Brahma, the startup combines blockchain, AI, IoT integrations and post-quantum security to capture and authenticate supply-chain data. Its flagship platform, BattMan, helps battery manufacturers track material origins, generate digital passports and manage regulatory compliance. LW3 is also targeting green hydrogen and e-fuel supply chains, where verifying product origins and carbon emissions is becoming important. The startup has secured a three-year contract with an undisclosed two-wheeler manufacturer and operates two hydrogen pilot sites. It has also received backing from the Algorand Foundation and Numaligarh Refinery's innovation ecosystem. With EU regulations set to mandate digital passports for specified batteries from February 2027, LW3 is targeting a battery passport market projected to reach $904.2 Mn by 2032. ________________________________________________________________________ Maasi | Bringing Structure To India’s Informal Nanny Market For working parents, finding a trustworthy nanny could be difficult. Neighbourhood referrals and WhatsApp recommendations offer little assurance about a caregiver's training, reliability or availability. Bengaluru-based Maasi wants to bring greater trust and convenience to this largely informal market. Founded by Aashu Manchali, Gargi Pandey and Reshov Roy, the startup connects families with verified, trained caregivers, offering on-demand nannies from ₹199 an hour and monthly subscriptions starting at ₹5,999. Its caregivers undergo training led by preschool directors, nurses and former airline cabin crew trainers. Maasi also offers English-speaking governesses trained in screen-free childcare activities. Having raised ₹6 Cr from Better Capital and Antler India in October, the startup plans to expand caregiver recruitment, training and Bengaluru operations. ________________________________________________________________________ NeuralMiles | Developing Retrofit Kits And Software Stacks For Heavy Industries Construction and mining are among the world's most equipment-intensive industries, yet much of their machinery still relies on human operators working long hours in hazardous conditions. What if these machines could operate remotely or even drive themselves? San Francisco-based NeuralMiles is looking to make this possible without requiring companies to replace their existing fleets. Founded in 2026 by Nakul Agarwal and Deep Boliya, who previously worked together on IIT Bombay Racing Driverless team's autonomous electric race car, the startup develops retrofit kits that enable remote operation and eventually autonomy in excavators. Its modular hardware connects to existing machine controls, including mechanical hydraulic systems, allowing operators to control equipment remotely. NeuralMiles has already demonstrated remote operation on a decade-old excavator. The startup operates on a teleoperation- and autonomy-as-a-service model, charging customers per excavator. Having raised $250K from Entrepreneurs First, NeuralMiles has secured contracts for real-site pilots and is targeting five deployments and over $1 Mn in contracted annual recurring revenue. However, scaling will depend on proving its technology can operate reliably across different machines, challenging worksites and varying connectivity conditions. ________________________________________________________________________ Nova Spectral | Making Infrared Vision More Affordable Conventional cameras struggle to capture clear images in darkness or through smoke, haze and dust. Short-wave infrared (SWIR) imaging can overcome some of these limitations, but the technology remains expensive, restricting its use largely to specialised defence and industrial applications. Bengaluru-based Nova Spectral AI wants to make this capability more accessible by developing lower-cost SWIR image sensor chips. Founded in 2026 by Anish Priyadarshi and Sanjeev Kumar, the startup is using lead-free indium arsenide colloidal quantum dots integrated with standard silicon CMOS technology. With this, the startup claims to make sensors up to 100 times cheaper than existing alternatives. Its initial focus is defence, drones and intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), with longer-term applications in robotics, autonomous vehicles, industrial inspection and consumer electronics.
